output: On April 23, a Russian SU-27 fighter flew close to a US RC-135U aircraft in the Sea of Okhotsk, performance considered aggressive, demonstrating its armed state, followed by US-Russian defense officials discussing the incident. This incident occurred amid ongoing tensions between the US and Russia concerning Russia's actions in Ukraine, where President Barack Obama has publicly condemned Russian aggression.

The Prince of Wales, Charles, and his wife Camilla are embarking on a 12-day tour to celebrate Charles' 67th birthday, visiting 12 different towns and cities across Australia and New Zealand, marking his 15th visit to Australia, with a possible meeting with the Australian Prime Minister.

A 70-year-old woman was attacked in Sneem, County Kerry, on September 20, while a man was detained and questioned at the Killarney Garda (police) station following an incident on a subsequent Saturday morning.
Hugh McGoldrick, a former GP, had his name removed from the medical register after admitting falsifying drug trials on sleep disorder patients, as no appeal was submitted within the 28-day deadline.
A 21-year-old is under police questioning on suspicion of murder, after a body was found in a wooded area in Dorking, Surrey, and the post-mortem results are pending.

Josh Hanson was stabbed and died at the RE bar in Eastcote, Hillingdon, around 1:10 BST on Sunday. Police are appealing for anyone who was in the bar after midnight or in the nearby area around 1:00 AM to come forward with information, as no arrests have been made in the case.

The article discusses a proposed new service between Sandown and Southsea, aimed at boosting tourism to the Isle of Wight, with the possibility of the service operating two days a week in July and August, subject to permits and discussions with local authorities.
A 30-year-old man was arrested following an attack by up to eight individuals on a victim in the Heights area at around 2 AM BST on Sunday, with police appealing for information about the incident.

In India, floods have caused the death of over 200 people in Assam, affected 450,000, and displaced many more. The Prime Minister plans to visit Assam to find a permanent solution to the annual flooding problem in the region.

The 25th anniversary season of the Premier League starts with Arsenal hosting Leicester City on Friday 11 August, with Sky Sports holding the rights to broadcast 10 Friday night matches, while a significant portion of football fans reported using unofficial online streams for matches.

Footballer Cristian Montano, aged 22, was dismissed by Oldham Athletic after a spot-fixing investigation by the National Crime Agency resulted in his arrest and suspension, a move deemed essential by the club in order to act swiftly and seriously.

A 20-year-old man was given a suspended jail sentence and supervision order for accidentally starting and causing extensive damage to a 42-acre former Pontins resort in Brixham, including the demolition of the arcade area, pool area, and ballroom, and increasing the demolition cost due to the presence of asbestos due to the fire's rapid spread.

Robert Wilson, a Scottish footballer, returned to Nottingham Forest from Celtic for £2.5m in 2013 for a second spell that lasted 51 appearances, but has been without a team since his release in May 2013.

Australia left-arm seamer Faulkner took 3-45 (dismissing Kusal Perera, Angelo Mathews, and Thisara Perera) in Colombo, where debutant slow left-armer Amila Aponso shone with 4-18. Matthew Wade's 76 was the top score for Australia, who were bowled out for 206 to lose by 82 runs and level the five-match series at 1-1. Other Australians with ODI hat-tricks are Bruce Reid, Anthony Stuart, Brett Lee, Clint McKay, and Dan Christian.

The 32-year-old Vadim Cobilas, a Sale rugby player, is out of contract in the summer and has decided to move to France's Top 14, with advance talks taking place to potentially fill his position. Some other players, including Chris Cusiter and Tommy Taylor, are reportedly considering their future options while Sale is actively recruiting for next season.

India were cruising towards 349 with centuries from Shikhar Dhawan and Virat Kohli, but collapsed from 277/1 to 323 all out in the third ODI, with Kane Richardson taking 5-68, and Australia taking the match 348-8 to 323 to lead the series 4-0, having won 18 consecutive ODIs on home soil.

The Hammersmith and City Line and partially the Circle Line have been temporarily suspended due to debris concerns caused by a fire in a 24-story building, at the request of the London Fire Brigade, with fears of a rising death toll of 58 victims.

Veteran Footballer Jamie Hamill, a 27-year-old who has previously played for Kilmarnock, returns to the club after a three-year stint at Hearts, marking his 150th appearance for Kilmarnock with a new three-year contract.
Ross Morgan, an excited Ipswich fan, accidentally punched a hole in the ceiling while celebrating Paul Anderson's goal against Norwich, with Anderson later offering to cover the repair costs.

Retailers in Wales are now compelled to hide tobacco products from public view, with fines and imprisonment possible for violations, in an effort to reduce visual access and thus discourage smoking, a decision backed by Public Health Wales.

The 20-year-old footballer named Lucas, who has previously played for the National League side and scored three goals in 10 appearances, is brought into the Bristol Rovers squad in League Two, with manager Luke Garrard suggesting he will provide options in the forward areas.

Knaresborough station in North Yorkshire is undergoing renovation, including waterproofing and removal/rebuild of the chimney stack on the signal box, with work primarily conducted at night to reduce disruption. The station, rich in history, is operated by Northern Rail.
Former NFL player Lawrence Phillips, known for his troubles both on and off the field, is believed to have committed suicide while serving a prison term for murder accusations.

The article discusses the extension of bus lane hours for Belfast Rapid Transit (BRT), starting at 7:00 and ending at 19:00, and a plan for two rounds of public consultation to design the system, considering factors like loading and unloading windows, to ensure efficient and user-friendly service, with operation scheduled for September 2018.

In a closely contested La Liga game, Messi seized the winner for Barcelona after being set up by Suarez, extending his record as the all-time La Liga top scorer, while Ronaldo moved up as Real Madrid's record league scorer in a separate match.

Over 70 individuals, including football players and directors from 30 clubs in lower Italian leagues, have been detained for allegations of "conspiracy to commit sporting fraud," with links to mafia organizations such as the 'Ndrangheta crime syndicate, and a local police officer is believed to be involved in the match-fixing scandal.

Spiderlings, hybrid species from Sussex and Suffolk, were released in Castle Marshes to increase genetic variability and adaptability in the new population, with the aim of helping them survive climate change impacts; this project was supported by Natural England, Suffolk Wildlife Trust, and the BBC Wildlife Fund.

The Partition of India in 1947 led to the formation of Pakistan and Bangladesh as independent countries and the displacement of millions, as related in the Newsround special "Finding My Family - Partition" on CBBC. (revised)

\- NONE. The summary accurately describes the events and program mentioned in the article.

Iva Barr, a seasoned marathon runner participating in her 20th marathon and having started with the first London Marathon in 1981, made a heartfelt decision to end her run early at the 14th mile, but was moved by the support of spectators, especially young people, along the route, vowing the experience would never be forgotten and expressing no regrets about her decision.

In China's top cities, the extreme competition in the property market has prompted some couples to resort to fake divorces to purchase additional homes, as the central bank's attempts to curb prices have had limited impact on affordability for young workers with low wages.

A 24-year-old individual is under arrest in connection with the suspicious death of Mr. Jones, a landlord, following a confrontation at a public house in Holyhead. The police are investigating and have released a family statement about Mr. Jones, who is described as a partner, soulmate, father, brother, and uncle. A post-mortem examination was conducted, but the cause of death has not been released yet. The police have requested information from individuals who were on a specific bus that passed through the Black Bridge area of Holyhead at the time of the incident.
The article invites readers to connect with BBC News Entertainment through various social media platforms, and encourages them to submit their story suggestions to a specific email address.

A red Ford Fiesta and a white Asda delivery van collided on the A713 near Carsphairn, causing the deaths of both drivers, Antony Sztuka and Scott Kennedy, who were from Ayrshire. Police are investigating and are particularly interested in a white flat-bed pickup truck that was on the road at the time of the crash.

Australian rowing champion Sarah Tait, who won a silver medal at the 2012 London Olympics with Kate Hornsey, was diagnosed with cervical cancer in 2013, serving as an inspiration to many young athletes in Australia, particularly female rowers. Heather Stanning, her British competitor from the Olympics, described Tait as an "incredible personality" and an inspiration for women in sports worldwide.

A suicide bomber, alleged by the Taliban, carried out two attacks in Kabul on the same day as the swearing-in of President Ashraf Ghani, injuring two soldiers, two civilians, and causing significant damage to an army bus in the west, and in the northeast, a claimed continuation of their offensive from the summer.

Daimler predicts significant growth in full-year sales, despite a slowdown in Mercedes sales in China, with confidence in continued growth in major emerging markets, although at a lower rate than last year, and a 6% increase in car and commercial vehicle sales in Q2.

A 10-year-old Danish prince was rescued from a dangerous rip current at Mermaid Beach by lifeguard Nick Malcolm, who could have prevented the boy's potential death, according to his supervisor Stuart Keay.

Emergency services responded to a nonsuspicious house fire on Elgin Road at 16:10 on Wednesday where an elderly man unfortunately perished, with no other injuries reported. A joint fire investigation was initiated.

Veterans with complex amputation-related medical issues in the UK are now receiving treatment at the Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre (DMRC) in Surrey, following the implementation of a system enabling tertiary referrals from NHS centers, leveraging the DMRC's decade-long expertise in managing military trauma injuries, thereby ensuring these veterans receive the highest quality care for their sacrifices.

Four speed enforcement cameras installed on a two-mile stretch of the M4 in Port Talbot, Wales, have resulted in about 125 drivers a day being caught speeding, marking a decrease from the 700 a day during a trial period in the area. While the decrease is welcomed, the Wales Road Casualty Reduction Partnership emphasizes that excessive speed remains a common cause of accidents and fatalities, and their priority is education over enforcement after considering engineering solutions.

A Manchester-born teacher living in Spain is under arrest for secretly taking and storing explicit photos of his underage students, some of which were shared online, as part of an Interpol investigation into illegal activities involving minors. Police are now trying to identify the victims in the images found on his electronic devices.

A seven-year-old sturgeon named Steve, once displayed at World of Water in Romsey, Hampshire, survived a flood and was later found at a nearby car wash. The center's manager reported the fish, which can sell for up to £1,000, had some scrapes but was otherwise healthy and eager to return to its display.

Chris Rock, the comedian and actor, has filed for divorce from his wife, Malaak, after 19 years of marriage, focusing on their family privacy; they share two daughters, the latest film starring Rock is a comedy about a comedian bystander in his own reality TV wedding.

A collision occurred on the motorway between Tamnamore, causing it to be shut down in both directions, resulting in significant traffic delays. Drivers traveling to Belfast are advised to exit at junction 15, while those heading to Enniskillen in County Fermanagh should exit at junction 12 and use Armagh city as an alternative route. Witnesses of the crash or those who saw the involved Honda Civic before the incident are asked to contact the police with information.

The French government has proposed senior diplomat Laurent Stefanini for the role of ambassador to the Vatican, aiming to improve relations with the more tolerant Pope Francis, but the Vatican has yet to respond or confirm the nomination, which is being viewed as a potential rejection due to the silence typically maintained by the Vatican in such cases.

The Nasdaq fell 2.4%, marking its biggest one-day drop since April 2021, driven mostly by declines in semiconductor and biotech stocks, despite a 35% rise in Kraft Foods after it agreed to merge with Heinz. The Dow Jones and S&P 500 also dropped significantly, while the US dollar weakened against the euro due to a decline in US durable goods orders.

Two underdogs had memorable victories in tennis tournaments: Marketa Vondrousova, the Czech world number 233, moved closer to the top 100 for the first time by beating Estonia's Kontaveit and Barbora Strycova to win a women's event; Borna Coric, the Croatian world number 79, saved five match points to defeat third-seeded Philipp Kohlschreiber and claim his first ATP title at the Grand Prix Hassan II in Marrakech.
Stoke City signs Cameroon International and former Schalke player, Eric Choupo-Moting, their fourth transfer of the summer, after previously trying to bring him to the club four years ago.

A man with cerebral palsy who was 56 and lived in a nursing home in Randalstown, Maine, died last September. The death was initially not treated as a murder case. However, after an autopsy, the investigation was reopened as a murder case, with a woman being questioned by police in April of this year.

Heavy rains have resulted in severe waterlogging, causing a city-wide standstill, school and office closures, and affected around 80,000 people in Sri Lanka, while triggering evacuations and rescues in India's Tamil Nadu state, with the chief minister announcing a relief fund for flood-affected areas, noting the unusually concentrated rainfall.

A McGill's 904 bus caught fire on the A760 Kilbirnie Road near Largs on Saturday, with the driver successfully evacuating all passengers without injury, as mentioned by one grateful passenger whose partially-sighted mother was on board. The road was closed, but it was later reopened after the burnt-out bus was removed.

Jake Ball, a 25-year-old bowler for Notts County, has taken a total of 6 wickets in each of their first two County Championship games, including a six-wicket haul in both, and is leading Notts' bowling attack alongside Stuart Broad. He has been praised by Mick Newell for his form and potential progression within the ECB setup. Despite his efforts, Notts lost their second County Championship match to Lancashire by 8 wickets.

A memorial stone made of Jersey granite, dedicated to the 120 Jersey men, known as "the Jersey Pals," who died during the Battle of the Somme, was unveiled in Guillemont, France, with a piece of the stone to be brought back to Jersey to form a part of a monument in Royal Square.

John Boyega, who played Finn in Star Wars: The Force Awakens and was a member of Theatre Peckham's company from age nine to 14, is currently filming Star Wars Episode Eight and expressed his honor to give back to the theatre, with its founder noting he'll be a significant inspiration for their young members.

In the European Tour event, Thailand's Aphibarnrat holds a one-shot lead with a birdie at the 14th, while Fitzpatrick, who led since day one, matches him with a birdie at the 15th. Donald, former world number one, scores a 65 and is four behind, while Westwood is two shots more back after a 67. Several players, including Donald, are within five strokes of the lead, with Welshman Bradley Dredge withdrawing due to illness.

In a strong partnership, Ashton Voges (128*) and Dawid Malan (147) scored big before Malan was dismissed, leaving Middlesex with a strong position in their County Championship game against Hampshire, with poor weather forecast threatening a draw for Hampshire.

A 52-year-old woman died and a 16-year-old boy is critically ill in hospital following an incident on Penilee Road, while police located a man they previously wanted to question in the Dumfries and Galloway area and have blocked off part of Penilee Road for forensic investigations.

The three-bedroom red brick terrace house at 9 Newcastle Road, Wavertree, once lived in by John Lennon from birth to age five, was sold to an anonymous bidder through a bidding war for an undisclosed amount, exceeding its guide price of £150,000 to £250,000, with significant interest from local and international buyers.

A man, Aaron Joseph, 29, denied owning a dog that attacked and eventually resulted in the death of David Ellam, 52, while walking his Yorkshire terrier last August in Sheepridge, Huddersfield. Joseph was bailed and the trial has been set for February 5, with a potential earlier trial date in hopes of the Recorder of Leeds, Judge Peter Collier QC. Joseph also pleaded guilty to possessing cannabis on the same day.
Twenty-two-year-old Thomas Bebbington, last seen entering a river near Dana Steps, was later found deceased, approximately 10 miles away from Shrewsbury.

Five-week-old otter cubs, unable to survive independently, are currently being cared for and fed multiple times daily, with hopes they'll mature enough to move to a spacious outdoor enclosure with live food during the summer.

A 33-year-old mother of four named Joanne Thompson was found dead at her Old Mill Court home in Newtownards on Wednesday, and police are investigating, requesting witnesses to a Monday bonfire disturbance, as well as anyone who saw activity around her house on Tuesday night and early Wednesday morning.

A record-breaking number of 2,270 black-tailed godwits restocked in a small field in Kilmoluaig, Hebrides, this spring, with a significant portion coming from Europe (France, Portugal, Spain), and bystanders reported that many were on their way to Iceland for breeding.

Rangers coach Jimmy Durrant will not be renewing his contract at Ibrox, as manager Mark Warburton plans to shake up the coaching staff, given Durrant's history at the club spanning 14 years as a player and coach, including roles with the first team under Walter Smith and Ally McCoist.
A rare albino deer is reported, estimated to occur once in 100,000 births, generating visitor interest as it adjusts to its new environment.

A 15-year-old boy named Asad Khan from Bradford died three weeks after starting at Beckfoot Upper Heath School, with his mother alleging he was bullied. During the inquest, it was revealed that Asad had expressed feelings of unsafe and thoughts to skip school, as well as comments about life being unfair. The coroner is considering calling a boy who may have information on the case, with the inquest set to resume next month.

The 1654 coronation ceremony painting, which has been hanging in Rokeby Park, Barnard Castle since 1880, is unique and valuable, but its origins and the artist responsible for its creation remain a mystery.

In the football match between Macclesfield Town and Wrexham, Macclesfield Town wins 3-0, with circumstances such as yellow cards for players Curtis Tilt and Jordan Evans, and several substitutions on each team. Macclesfield Town places seventh in the table, while Wrexham remains 15th.

The African Football Confederation (Caf) has agreed a sponsorship deal with French oil and gas company Total, marking Total's takeover from Orange as the headline sponsor for the next phase of 10 Caf competitions, aiming to further the development of African football and strengthen Total's ties to stakeholders and customers in Africa.

Spain coach Lopetegui has recalled Diego Costa, Juan Mata, and David de Gea, as well as defenders Sergio Ramos, Dani Carvajal, Gerard Pique, Jordi Alba, Marc Bartra (a defender), Javi Martinez, and Cesar Azpilicueta, and midfielders Sergi Roberto, Sergio Busquets, Saul Niguez, Koke, Marco Asensio, Lucas Vazquez, Thiago Alcantara, David Silva, and Juan Mata, for a friendly match against Belgium and a World Cup qualifier against Liechtenstein. The squad includes three goalkeepers, eight defenders (including Marc Bartra and Cesar Azpilicueta), and six midfielders. However, the article does not specify whether there are any additional defenders or any specific defender other than Marc Bartra.

A large, deliberately-started wildfire spanning a 5km area has occurred near the border of two regions, with 45 firefighters struggling to contain it, as it's the latest out of 435 wildfires since early May, and officials are urging the public to stop setting fires due to the risks to both property and lives.

Ireland cricketer Boyd Rankin, 31, returns to the national team after a hiatus, citing a lack of opportunities with England in the last two years, and expressed eagerness to help Ireland potentially achieve Test status. He is eligible to play for Ireland again as per ICC regulations from January 18, 2016, and will participate in the InterContinental Cup match with Papua New Guinea in early February, as well as the upcoming World Twenty20 tournament in India.

The Northern Ireland Rare Disease Partnership, initiated by the Patient Client Council, seeks to provide an independent voice for sufferers and their carers of rare diseases, with a focus on education, special services, and support, aiming to advocate on their behalf and enhance treatment and care.

Gloucester Cathedral announces its plan to open its choral group to girls for the first time, aiming to find talented youth from diverse backgrounds and encouraging participation through an open day and auditions.

Chelsea winger Pedro, age 29, was hospitalized after sustaining an injury in the 3-0 win against Beijing, suffered a concussion, and required overnight observation. He is expected to wear a protective mask during his return to training, while the rest of the Chelsea squad moves on to Singapore for two upcoming games.

Former England cricketer James Taylor (27), who retired due to a heart condition in 2016, is now working with Nottinghamshire and Yorkshire's academies, offering one-day cricket experiences to their batsmen. Additionally, former Northants captain David Sales, who is known for his impressive batting statistics, is working with Nottinghamshire's batsmen, focusing on improving technical aspects of their game based on his cricket brain and experience.

A man was charged with criminal damage, disorderly behavior, and assault on police after allegedly causing a disturbance on Whiterock Road at 15:00 GMT on a Friday, which was witnessed by people picking up prescriptions, including children, and is set to appear in court on 5 December.

A yacht's engine failed a mile north-east of Muck Island on Thursday evening, prompting a volunteer crew from Larne RNLI to launch two lifeboats in good weather conditions to tow the yacht to Carrick Marina, demonstrating effective collaboration between the inshore and all-weather lifeboats.

In the match between Ipswich and MK Dons, David McGoldrick scored his first goal since August, Brett Pitman and Josh Murphy contributed one each, while Revell netted twice from spot-kicks and an assist to equalize, ultimately leading to Ipswich's victory; post-match, Ipswich's manager Mick McCarthy found the game exhilarating for the fans but frustrating for himself, while MK Dons' manager Karl Robinson lamented the team's inconsistency and poor performance in key areas, with both managers reflecting on preparations for the next season.

A pedestrian bridge collapsed on a London-bound motorway near Maidstone on August 27, causing serious injury to one motorcyclist, resulting in a man from Darlington facing multiple charges, including dangerous driving, and the road was closed twice for debris removal, affecting the main route to the Channel Tunnel and Port of Dover.

Holidaymakers in Platja d'Aro were seized with panic after a flashmob consisting of individuals pretending to be paparazzi caused a stampede, mistaking selfie sticks for weapons. Police were called, resulting in eleven injuries and three hospitalizations, with organizers, German women, being detained for public order offences.

Two individuals, Sindyann Regis and Chevaze Mcgregor, are charged with the murder of a 2.5-year-old boy, Jeremiah Regis, from Wolverhampton, who died from abdominal peritonitis caused by blunt force trauma. The court heard that Jeremiah had over 100 injuries, including a bite to the chest.

A gorse fire on Woodbury Common in Devon spread over a large area due to high winds, resulting in four people being treated for smoke inhalation, one being hospitalized with burns, and triggering an overnight response from fire services. Evacuations were conducted at the nearby Woodbury Park Golf and Country Club, and the public was advised to avoid the area.

The British Speedway Promoters' Association has reached an agreement to secure the club's future, including a 15-year lease for the Beaumont Park venue, according to Keith Chapman, the association's chairman. Further meetings are needed to set up the club's management structure, schedule a 2017 season race, and finalize other arrangements.

A 50-year-old woman, Elizabeth Bowe, died three days after being badly injured at Bobby Jones Place in St Andrews, and her 51-year-old brother, Charles Gordon, has been charges with murder; the Police Investigations and Review Commissioner (PIRC) has ordered an investigation into the initial police response leading up to the incident.

A 29-year-old footballer, Jim O'Brien, has signed a two-year deal with Ross County after a brief loan period last season, where he made 18 appearances and scored twice. His return is hoped to provide valuable experience to the younger players and contribute to the team's development, although his availability for the upcoming Scottish League Cup match may be dependent on international clearance.

In Division Two cricket, Northants seized early advantages against Durham with regular wickets, dismissing top scorer Michael Richardson, Paul Collingwood, Keaton Jennings, and others for the low total of 103. Despite a fightback by Durham's Barry McCarthy, Northants ended the day struggling at 59-3, 107 runs behind. Durham's fragile batting lineup was exposed by Northants' seam attack after their recent dramatic defeat by Glamorgan.

A 19-year-old New Zealander trails by one shot the joint leaders Brooke Henderson and Lee Mi-rim after round two of the Sahalee Country Club event, with the Canadian Henderson struggling and South Korea's Lee excelling, while Catriona Matthew of Scotland is three strokes back after a strong round on a challenging day. Only a handful of players are at par or better at the halfway stage, with Lydia Ko expressing gratitude for her putter keeping her in contention.

Former footballer Steve Watson, 56, will rejoin Scotland's coaching staff as assistant to manager Gordon Strachan, having formerly worked under Alex McLeish during the Euro 2008 qualifying campaign. Watson, who played with Strachan and Mark McGhee at Aberdeen, expressed enthusiasm for the opportunity to help Scotland in their World Cup qualifiers. He had previously left the Scotland team to become manager of Bradford City.

A hockey match between Belfast Giants and Braehead Clan saw Belfast Giants win 5-1, with goals from Colin Shields, Ryan Martinelli, Mark Garside, Alex Foster, and Steve Saviano, while Braehead Clan's only goal was scored by Scott Aarssen on the powerplay. Belfast Giants have a game in hand on their rivals, Devils, who won on the same day.

Jordan Spieth, the defending Masters champion, suffered a dramatic collapse on the final day of the tournament, culminating in a quadruple-bogey seven on the par-three 12th. Danny Willett capitalized on this, becoming the first Englishman since Nick Faldo in 1996 to win the event. Faldo, a three-time Masters winner, described Spieth's collapse as a scarring and damaging experience, noting similarities with Greg Norman's collapse in 1996.

The article details instructions on how to submit photographs to England's Big Picture project by email, social media, or Instagram, emphasizing the use of recent images, adherence to BBC's Terms and Conditions, and retaining the copyright to submitted content while granting the BBC a non-exclusive license to use the materials.

Eye specialist Honey Rose is on trial for gross negligence manslaughter, accused of failing to detect serious swollen optic discs during a routine eye test on Vincent Barker (Vinnie), leading to his untimely death five months later.

Food price inflation increased to 4.9% in June, primarily due to rising pork prices, remaining below the target figure of 3.5%, and this might impede potential interest rate cuts in 2013 due to economic concerns and the risk of fueling a property bubble. The anticipated growth rate for China's economy in 2013 is expected to be 7.5%, which would be the slowest rate in 23 years.

Ivorian footballer Cheick Tiote, aged 30, passed away following a collapse during training with Chinese second-tier side Beijing Enterprises on 5 June. His memorial service was attended by friends, family, and former team-mates, including Senegal striker Papiss Cisse, who shared emotional memories of their time together at Newcastle United. Over his seven-year tenure at the English club, Tiote made over 150 appearances, and had recently joined Beijing Enterprises in February.

In the fifth stage of the race, Slovak rider Peter Sagan won the uphill sprint, with Thibaut Pinot moving to second overall, while Nairo Quintana maintained the lead. British rider Geraint Thomas moved up to sixth overall, with two stages remaining.
Cuadrilla secures approval for its fracking plans in Lancashire, promising local jobs, investment, and community benefits, but opponents have initiated a legal challenge.

Three unnamed teenage boys from north-west London, suspected of planning to travel to Syria, were arrested upon their return to the UK at Istanbul's Sabiha Gokcen airport, detained after flying from Barcelona, Spain. They were later released without charge. Their arrest follows the international manhunt for three east London schoolgirls who took flights to Istanbul and are believed to have joined IS militants in Syria.

A respiratory consultant, Dr. Christopher Davies, criticism a hospital's expenditure on purchasing a blackout blind for £22.95, stating it was fitted for free by in-house staff, while a hospital spokesperson stated the quote was reviewed and rejected, leading to questions about NHS funding.

Adam King was instrumental in Swansea City's 2-0 win over Reading in March, and the Swans' development squad clinched the league title with a draw against Wolverhampton Wanderers, achieving 31 wins throughout the 2016-17 season, while the senior team was able to stay in the Premier League despite Hull's relegation due to Crystal Palace's 4-0 victory over them on Sunday.

December 2013 storms damaged a dune system east of Barkby Beach in Prestatyn, with natural re-establishment observed but concerns remain due to narrowness. The Denbighshire council is considering creating a secondary dune system to strengthen defenses against flooding, following a flood risk management report suggesting discussions with Natural Resources Wales to potentially create a secondary dune system on the landward side of the existing dunes. Approximately 400 residents were displaced from their homes in Rhyl, one of the hardest-hit areas, where hundreds of properties were left without power during the storm.

South Shields (8th tier of English football), who successfully played at Wembley last season, will host a live FA Cup game against Bridlington Town, streamed across BBC Sport's digital platforms on August 19, with commentary from Conor McNamara and Danny Webber, who will interact with the audience via the #bbcfacup hashtag.

Police are investigating a targeted attack on Craigmillar Castle Road, where a 38-year-old man suffered serious, but non-life threatening, facial injuries, while a 49-year-old man did not require medical attention. Police Scotland is asking for witnesses and information about any suspicious behavior or vehicles in the area around the time of the incident.

A 51-year-old woman, Pamela McLaggan, pleaded guilty to manslaughter after the death of 44-year-old Jonathan Baines, known as "Willy," at a house on Ropery Road, Gainsborough, following an outing to Market Rasen races and town pubs, and will be sentenced on December 21 at Lincoln Crown Court.

A 15-year-old boy was attacked by a couple in their 40s at Patterton station, suffering facial injuries including an eye injury, and lost his mobile phone in the incident. The assault occurred on a 23:05 service between Glasgow Central and Neilston, with witnesses urged to contact British Transport Police if they have relevant information.

A 17-year-old from Dewsbury was questioned under the Terrorism Act in April regarding potential ties to Islamic State, and the West Yorkshire Police are currently investigating him and another missing teen, Hassan Munshi, who is the younger brother of a previous terrorism act convict.

The article announces that GB's ice hockey team, featuring three forwards and a goalie, will compete in a qualifying tournament against Italy, Netherlands, and Serbia to reach the final qualifying stage for the 2018 Winter Games in PyeongChang, with a significant overlap in players from the 2015 World Championship (Division 1B) silver medal-winning squad. Additionally, an Italian team, Cortina, will play against the Belfast Giants as part of the 'Olympic Series' during the tournament.

Matthew Perry may participate in a tribute to the show's creator, James Burrows, but it is not a reunion of the Friends cast as originally expected, with Jennifer Aniston, Courteney Cox, Lisa Kudrow, David Schwimmer, and Matt LeBlanc participating. The special will air on NBC on 21 February, and Friends ended in 2004. Matthew Perry is also set to star in a play titled The End of Longing in London's West End, running from 2 February until 14 May.

Veteran footballer Jones, who began his career at Manchester United and played for multiple clubs, including Wigan, made 41 appearances in the previous season to help Burnley win the Championship, and continued to start for them in their Premier League match against Swansea.

A renowned lawyer from Melbourne's Italian community, who had represented crime bosses accused of various offenses, was murdered, with authorities suspecting that underworld figures may have targeted him due to a potential bounty on his head, with renewed gangland tensions still present in Melbourne.

An Air France 777-200 en route from Paris to Vancouver was diverted to Prestwick, Scotland, due to a slight smell of burning on board, and a second aircraft was sent to transport passengers back to Charles de Gaulle Airport.

The Met Office has issued a severe weather warning, predicting strong winds and heavy rain as Hurricane Gonzalo reaches Britain on Monday night, particularly affecting coastal areas and north-western parts of Wales, with potentially damaging gusts exceeding 55mph inland and up to 70mph by exposed coastal areas, also canceling some Irish Ferries sailings between Holyhead and Dublin due to adverse weather forecasts.

The article discusses concerns about hospital overcrowding, as told by Jenny, who spoke to a doctor in a children's hospital in Sheffield, and shared the experiences of patients Lilly and Jake, who had to wait extended periods due to overcrowding and subsequent wait times before being treated.

A 34-year-old man was charged with causing grievous bodily harm, a 57-year-old woman was bailed on charges of grievous bodily harm with intent and perverting the course of justice, and Kenneth David Dickie, 64, died from a serious head injury he sustained at the Rockley Park site in Poole, Dorset.

Former Manchester United forward Federico Macheda will remain at Nottingham Forest until the end of the season, while David Vaughan has signed a one-year contract, but Andre Moritz will not join the club due to complications with his contract at Thai Premier League side Buriram United.

Two others, Ken Cresswell, 57, and John Shaw, 61, remain missing, and a fourth body, Michael Collings, had been previously recovered. The Swansea East MP Carolyn Harris expressed her sadness for the affected family and emphasized the remaining uncertainty and ongoing wait for the other two families.

Bosnia-Herzegovina's international player is working to regain full fitness after a hernia injury, while QPR may miss midfielder Jordan Cousins for the rest of the season due to a quadricep injury. On-loan winger Kazenga LuaLua is back in training for QPR after an ankle injury but remains a doubt. Bristol City is aiming for a win over QPR on Friday to move ahead of other teams in the league standings.

Italian astronaut Luca Parmitano, trained by the European Space Agency (ESA), expressed profound joy during his 2013 mission to the International Space Station, where he conducted two spacewalks, orbited Earth 2,656 times, and traveled over 110 million km.

The 16-year-old England Knights player, Joe Arundel, expressed excitement and a touch of nervousness about his debut with Hull FC, with the club's director of rugby acknowledging that Arundel's potential and long-term career prospects align with Hull FC's and England's focus on building a strong and enduring culture and winning mentality.

Ulster Bank is urgently working to rectify an issue causing payment delays for about 600,000 customers, aiming to resolve it by Saturday, with assurances that no customers will be left out of pocket; this situation is a repeat of a similar 2012 IT failure affecting more than 6.5 million customers, for which the bank group has since invested heavily to improve its computer systems.
In the 2016 Women's Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, Tanzania secured a 2-1 victory over Kenya, while Ethiopia defeated Uganda 4-1 in the play-off for third place.

McDonald's Japan is rationing French fries due to reduced supplies caused by industrial action among American west coast dockworkers affecting over 3,100 outlets; this comes after a butter shortage affected supermarkets this month.

Atletico Madrid's top scorer, Antoine Griezmann, has a haematoma on his left foot, ruled out a bone injury, and will miss France's friendly against Ivory Coast due to treatment, potentially hindering Atletico as they prepare to face league leaders Real Madrid in their next game.

Former Australian rugby league star Willie Mason, who had a 15-year career with five clubs including Canterbury, where he won a Premiership, and had an international career with Australia and the Kangaroos, has joined Super League club Toulouse for the 2022 season and has been praised by coach Laurent Frayssinous for his physical and aggressive playing style. Toulouse have started the 2022 season with two losses.

The new survey indicates a significant increase in dog feces on UK beaches, particularly in Scotland, raising health concerns due to bacteria present. Volunteers found that many pet owners use plastic bags to clean up waste, but the Marine Conservation Society now seeks to encourage more disposal of bags in provided dog bins. The survey also notes a decrease in overall litter levels on beaches this year.

In a League Two match, Wycombe Wanderers defeated Dagenham & Redbridge 3-1 after Josh Passley was given a red card for a tackle on Garry Thompson and Garry Thompson was sent off for a challenge on Joss Labadie. Scorers for Wycombe were Paul Hayes, Luke Guttridge, and Paris Cowan-Hall, while Guttridge scored for Dagenham & Redbridge. Wycombe moved up to sixth place in the table, above Leyton Orient on goal difference. Despite the loss, Dagenham & Redbridge manager John Still expressed optimism about the team's potential, citing good energy levels and a strong performance despite going down a man.

Bee-eaters, native to southern Europe, successfully bred a second consecutive summer in Low Gelt Quarry, near Brampton, creating nesting tunnels in the quarry banks, drawing over a thousand visitors to an RSPB viewpoint, and are expected to leave the nest in approximately four weeks.

A man disappeared after his kayak capsized in a fast-flowing, flood-warned River Wey in Guildford, with a boy's attempt to save him hindered by onlookers. Emergency services responded, and divers are currently searching the river, while public is urged not to enter the water and call 999 if they spot the missing kayaker. The river near Thames Lock is popular with kayakers, including the Wey Valley Kayak Club that issued a warning about the unsafe conditions earlier in the day.

A young girl died after an unusual behavior by an elephant resulted in a stone getting past its enclosure and hitting her at an unnamed zoo. The events were filmed by a bystander and uploaded onto YouTube.

MP for North West Durham, Ms. Glass, joins the wave of Labour MP resignations, questioning the leadership of Mr. Corbyn due to his position becoming "untenable." Her predecessor, Ms. Powell, has also stepped down and cited Mr. Corbyn's inability to effectively lead the opposition as a key reason for her resignation.

Chelsea currently lead the English Premier League with 59 points, with both Tottenham and Manchester United close behind, suggesting a competitive race for the title with six teams in contention. Chelsea face a challenging match against in-form Burnley, emphasizing the importance of focus and concentration for every game.

Police and community support officers in Llangefni have implemented a dispersal order to address recurring issues of antisocial behavior, alcohol consumption, and criminal damage among young adults. The order allows them to remove troublemakers and take those under 16 to a place of safety, with potential bans of up to 24 hours or arrest for return to the area. The aim is to reassure residents and protect young people from excessive alcohol use and its consequences.

Dutch midfielder Marten de Roon, 26, spent a year in the Premier League with Middlesbrough scoring five goals in 36 games, and Middlesbrough manager Garry Monk has identified Chelsea's Lewis Baker as a potential signing target for the Championship club this summer.

The Roald Dahl Funny Prize, which honors authors and artists of humorous children's books, will be relaunched in 2016 as part of the author's centenary celebrations, aiming to make it even more impactful and ensuring a robust future for this unique celebration of funny books.

Frazier Glenn Miller Jr, convicted of capital murder and hate crimes, was sentenced to death for targeting Jewish sites in Kansas, with the judge stating that his attempt to spread hate has failed. Miller responded with a "heil Hitler" before being removed, expressing that he was content with the death sentence as he believed in killing Jews as they hold too much power.

The city council plans to launch a larger self-service bike scheme in April 2017 with 500 bikes positioned across the city, inspired by the success of London's 'Boris bikes.' The scheme, financed through sponsorship, aims to provide bikes at easily accessible sites like district centers, universities, and strategic locations near public transport facilities.

The article discusses that Senegal international Sakho, who has only played twice all season due to a back injury and initial season start, is now undergoing light training following surgery, and will need several weeks of pre-season work to rebuild strength and fitness to potentially play in the Premier League again.

The Northern Ireland Residential Property Price Index for Q3 2021 shows an annual increase in property prices by up to 7.3%, with terraced houses having the largest annual rise (7.1%) and the fewest increases seen in apartments (4%), with over 5,200 deals completed. However, compared to Q2 2021, prices remained almost flat with a 0.8% rise.

The article discusses how deliveries of massive wind turbine parts on rural roads in Dumfries and Galloway have resulted in varying outcomes, with one successful passage and another ending in the lorry and its cargo ending up in a ditch.

The Betsi Cadwaladr health board is holding public consultations on possible temporary downgrades of maternity care services at Glan Clwyd Hospital and other district hospitals due to staffing shortages, prompted by a previous legal challenge, with residents expressing concern about the potential increase in travel for mothers seeking care, while health officials argue the changes are necessary for the safety of mothers and babies and a dedicated health board website has been launched for public feedback, with meetings scheduled for September.

Mignon du Preez scored a powerful century (116 off 99 balls) with crucial partnerships from Chloe Tryon (52) and Luisa Zoet (52), as South Africa reached 272-6. Despite Ireland's openers falling early to Masabata Klaas, Clare Shillington and Mary Waldron contributed forties, but South Africa's spinners, including Klaas, Sune Luus, and Yolani Fourie, took multiple wickets to dismiss Ireland for 204.
British high jumper Lisa Peake, aged 30, aims to break her own Welsh high jump record and qualify for Team GB in Rio by clearing 4.50m at the upcoming competition in Cardiff.

A deliberate arson attack caused a large fire at a building site involving scrapped railway sleepers, which took more than 10 hours to put out in Llanwern, and the incident is currently under police investigation.

The Nepal Scotland Association held a charity event in Edinburgh, Scotland, featuring a Singing Bowl Concert at St Giles' Cathedral, to raise funds for the Nepal earthquake relief effort, as they have lost many loved ones in the disaster.

Neil Lennon, Hibernian's head coach, was suspended by UEFA's control, ethics and disciplinary body for remonstrating with officials during a Europa League qualifier, after a goal was disallowed. The club is appealing the suspension.

A fire broke out 1,100 meters under the sea bed at the ICL UK Boulby mine, causing seven workers to be hospitalized for smoke inhalation. The Health and Safety Executive served an improvement notice to the company, with 11 workers initially unaccounted for, and the investigation is ongoing.

Two British tourists, Adam Burton and an unidentified French tourist, were questioned for minor offenses against morality after being caught naked at the Machu Picchu Unesco World Heritage site. The Peruvian authorities are in contact with the UK's Foreign Office regarding the incident.

Ivan Rakitic, a 28-year-old Croatia international and current Barcelona player, will finalize a new contract with a £109m buyout clause on Friday, extending his stay with the La Liga champions until 2021.

A couple in Halstead, UK suffered severe injuries in an alleged two-hour torture incident on 26 April, during a home invasion. The attackers, including one tall black man and two white men, escaped with an undisclosed sum of cash. authorities have obtained a detailed description of one suspect, continuing the investigation for the perpetrators of this horrific crime.

On July 25-26 at East Kirkcarswell Farm near Dundrennan, Scotland, the Wickerman Festival will feature a diverse lineup with Dizzee Rascal as the opening night headliner. Other acts include Martha Reeves and The Vandellas, The Zombies, Big Country, and The Feeling. The organizers are excited about the event and are planning to announce more acts, including the Saturday night headliner, in the coming weeks.

English rugby players Foden (Saints) and Brown (Quins), both 26, are performing exceptionally well in the Aviva Premiership, increasing expectations for them to be recalled to the England squad for the Six Nations tournament, with Foden optimistic about the possibility of multiple Saints players being included.

A 22-year-old motorcyclist died, and a 10-year-old boy remains in a serious condition following a collision between a KTM motorcycle and a Vauxhall Zafira in Dagenham, Essex. No arrests have been made, and police are seeking witnesses to the incident.

Pfizer has agreed to acquire California-based Anacor Pharmaceuticals, whose flagship product, the eczema cream crisaborole, is awaiting US FDA approval, aiming to address a significant unmet medical need for eczema patients and potentially achieve $2bn in annual sales, according to Pfizer's estimates. The announcement follows Pfizer's recent termination of a planned $160bn merger with Allergan.

Police were called to Oxlow Lane, Dagenham, at 23:00 BST on Saturday due to a street fight. Officers recovered multiple weapons and cannabis from the crowd, made two arrests (one for possession of an offensive weapon, another for assaulting police), and no one was injured. Insp Jason O'Donohue stated that by recovering the knives, the officers helped prevent another tragedy.
A 23-year-old man from Cardiff was arrested on suspicion of sexual assault after an early morning attack on a 19-year-old woman at Gorsedd Gardens near the Cardiff Civic Centre.

Conservative MSP John Lamont resigned his Ettrick, Roxburgh, and Berwickshire constituency seat to challenge SNP's Calum Kerr in a Westminster by-election, with the Liberal Democrats putting forward Catriona Bhatia as their by-election candidate.

The EU Commission has announced that countries including the UK, Ireland, France, and Germany can now sell beef to Canada, marking a step forward amid struggling farm sectors due to a Russian import ban and weaker Chinese demand, with the EU's successful measures to eradicate BSE and a €500m aid package previously announced.

The European Commission is planning to sanction countries on a tax blacklist for not complying with changes in tax haven usage, as revealed by the Panama Papers leak. Negotiations for a common EU list of non-cooperative jurisdictions and the implementation of an agreement for the exchange of information on company beneficial owners and a crackdown on offshore banking and tax advisory services are ongoing.

Discoveries made during the construction of the West Link in Inverness include Bronze Age burnt mounds, pottery fragments, and remains of kilns used for drying grain, likely relics of a community using heated stones to heat water for cooking, washing wool, or small saunas.

In a League One match, Oldham Athletic secured victory over Southend United, with standout moments including a goal by Main, a saved shot by David Worrall, and misses by Jonathan Forte and Tareiq Holmes-Dennis for Southend, leaving Oldham six points clear of relegation zones with three games remaining, while Southend remain in 13th place.

Irish actor Maírtin Lally, best known for his roles in Glenroe, Ballykissangel, and several Irish language films, passed away peacefully in hospital after a short illness. Survived by his wife Peggy and their children, he also had notable roles in a Hollywood movie and an Oscar-nominated animated film.

Derby City Council initially wanted to close Moorways Pool to save £350,000 yearly, but later decided to keep it open for a year due to necessary cuts and job restructuring, as the remaining public pool for teaching young swimmers in the city.

The article reports that children, previously held captive by Boko Haram, were detained without given ages or length in a military barracks in Maiduguri, with concerns raised by human rights groups about their treatment. Meanwhile, 21 Chibok schoolgirls were recently released from Boko Haram captivity.

Alexander suffered a broken cheekbone in a victory over Rangers, potentially hindering his subsequent performances, while Lee Hollis, with experience at Motherwell, is being considered as a replacement for another Hearts goalkeeper, Neil, who is injured, with doubts surrounding his availability for the upcoming Edinburgh derby.

Basketball player Chelsey Lee, 26, is under investigation for allegedly fabricating her and her father's birth certificates to qualify as a foreign player in the Women's Korean Basketball League(WKBL), where teams are allowed only two foreign players. Her team Bucheon KEB Hana Bank faces annulment of records, league rule changes, and the departure of the owner and head coach due to this scandal.

The article discusses an app that assesses Wi-Fi performance and identifies potential sources of interference, according to Ofcom statistics revealing slow Wi-Fi speeds in many homes and offices, poor broadband access in rural areas and small businesses, and increased use of catch-up TV, online film rental services, and video calls with the widespread availability of super-fast broadband.

The article discusses how Manchester United player Paul Pogba used social media to express his feelings after a draw with Liverpool, while teammate Zlatan Ibrahimovic equated social media pressure to the top-tier competitive environment and emphasized his focus on team success rather than individual accolades.

A 73-year-old man discovered a large, car-sized metal object on a river in Salinopolis, Brazil, that was later identified as debris from Europe's largest telecommunications satellite, Alphasat, launched from French Guiana last July. The debris, marked with the UK Space Agency and Arianespace logos, likely originated from the launch vehicle payload shroud and is believed to have floated inland from the Atlantic. Authorities plan to collect the object after initial disbelief and delays in response to reports of the find.

A former BBC executive warns that the decriminalization of non-payment of TV licence could cost £200m, potentially impacting low-income households and leading to the closure of BBC Four, CBBC, and CBeebies, and could not be discussed before the BBC's charter renewal talks in 2017. Meanwhile, a parliamentarian has called on the BBC to reverse its decision to close BBC Three as a television channel, raising concerns over job losses and the loss of popular programming, and advocating for a licence fee increase to track inflation during the charter renewal.

Derry City struggles against Finn Harps, conceding two goals to Ryan Curran and David Scully during the match, with Jordan Allan and Rory Patterson managing responses, but ultimately falling short in recovering the deficit, marking Harps' first win over Derry since 1998 and their return to the Premier Division since 2008.

The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has mandated that issuers of securities based on distributed ledger or blockchain technology, such as Initial Coin Offerings (ICOs), must register offers and sales, aiming to protect investors and maintain market integrity.

Operation Anagram, formed by Strathclyde Police in 2006, was instrumental in convicting serial killer Peter Tobin of raping and murdering Angelika Kluk, as well as the murders of Dinah McNicol and Vicky Hamilton. The operation, while being scaled back, has brought closure to some bereaved families and will continue to investigate any new information regarding Tobin's potential involvement in other unsolved crimes. Tobin is currently serving three life sentences for these murders.

In the Australian Grand Prix, Ferrari's Sebastian Vettel emerged victorious over Lewis Hamilton, with the latter hoping for a turnaround at the Chinese Grand Prix as both acknowledge the close competition between their teams, with Vettel admitting beating Mercedes is no easy feat.

During the Southwark Crown Court trial, it was reported that Mr Clifford, a former high-profile agent, is accused of indecent assault in the 1980s. The alleged victim claims he forced her to perform a sex act, threatened rape or murder, and exposed himself. She also alleges that he put her hand on his penis, to which he replied "no comment" during a police interview. His trial has been adjourned until Monday, with the majority of his interview responses being "no comment." Notably, Mr Clifford was a successful agent representing several notable celebrities including Simon Cowell, Jade Goody, and Muhammad Ali.

Ospreys coach Steve Tandy anticipates a high-scoring, physically demanding match against Scarlets on Boxing Day, with Nicky Smith available to play and hopes to close the 14-point gap in the Pro12 table. New Zealand scrum-half Brendon Leonard remains doubtful with a shoulder injury.

The annual Diwali celebration on Leicester's Belgrave Road, also known as the Golden Mile, attracted a massive crowd with fireworks, street art, and stage performances for the celebration of light over darkness. One of the largest such events outside of India, it welcomed diverse audiences and fostered unity, with circumstances such as food exchanges, family prayers, and shared joy transcending religious lines. Furthermore, additional Diwali-themed events took place throughout the city, including arts and crafts at Newarke Houses Museum and Gardens and shows at Curve theatre. Lastly, traffic restrictions were implemented on Belgrave Road and Belgrave Flyover during the festivities.

Rosie's Helping Hands, a charity founded by the parents of Rosie Ross who was tragically killed in 2001, has raised over £350,000 for young people in Aldridge. After 16 years, the family has decided to wind down the charity, with the last annual fundraiser, Rosie's Walk, occurring on Sunday at Aldridge Airfield. They plan to continue fundraising and helping projects until summer 2017, having previously funded a pirate themed play area on the children's ward at Walsall Manor Hospital, which greatly improved the space for sick children.

Macmillan Cancer Support plans to invest £5m in a new palliative care unit at the Llantrisant site, aiming to provide inpatient, outpatient, and day care for incurable cancer and other conditions, ensuring easier access to specialist tests and treatments for patients in the county, and the unit is expected to open in late 2018 or early 2019.

The article discusses North Wales, UK, being named the fourth best region to visit in the world, according to Lonely Planet, attracting more tourists and contributing to the Welsh government's economy targets. Places mentioned include Snowdonia, Conwy, and ZipWorld's zip-line over Penrhyn Quarry in Methesda.

The Columba Declaration, jointly authored by a Presbyterian Kirk minister and the Church of England's Bishop of Chester, aims to strengthen communication and partnership between the Church of England and the Church of Scotland, recognizing each other formally for the first time. The agreement establishes a 'light-touch' contact group to facilitate clergy and laypeople's movement between the two Churches, acknowledging their distinct constitutional roles within the UK. The discussion about the declaration will take place in the Church of England's General Synod in February and the Church of Scotland's General Assembly in May.

British Army veteran Ben Parkinson, who was badly injured in a bomb attack in Afghanistan in 2006, received an overwhelming number of friend requests on Facebook during his torch-bearing run, reaching the 5,000 limit for personal pages. His mother mentioned that his page had 19,000 hits, and he has also received hundreds of visit requests with the Olympic torch, firmly displaying public support for him. Facebook advises him to move towards a page instead of a profile if he continues to attract such attention.

At Beirut's airport, a large-scale drug smuggling operation was uncovered involving individuals who were reportedly detained but not identified, resulting in the seizure of two tonnes of Captagon pills, widely consumed in the Middle East and a significant contributor to conflicts, particularly in Syria.

The Sexual Offences, Exploitation and Child Abuse Command is investigating allegations against Kids Company, a charity founded and run by Camila Batmanghelidjh that provides support to some of the most deprived and vulnerable inner-city children; the charity emphasizes that its priority is the safety of its clients and has robust policies and procedures in place to protect them, reporting any allegations of misconduct to the police if necessary.

The Queen, who turns 90 this week, is reported to have a diverse range of accent adaptations, including a hilarious Norfolk brogue and an impressive Scottish accent, and is known for her sense of humor and ability to tell amusing anecdotes, like the time a shopper mistook her for the Queen on one of her trips to Sandringham.

The UN Agency for Human Settlements report shows that income inequality in Latin America is extremely high, with the richest 20% earning 20 times more than the poorest 20%. The region is the world's most urbanised, and by 2050, nearly nine out of 10 Latin Americans will live in cities. The report suggests that Latin American nations use the current period of relative economic stability and slower population growth to make life in cities more equitable and to address the high rate of labor informality, particularly affecting young people and women.

A Carmarthenshire Labour councillor is under investigation after it appears that she shared a post from Britain First that potentially advocated capital punishment for sex offenders, contradicting her opposition to the death penalty. The controversy stems from her stance against the council's plan to remove English-stream education at Ysgol Llangennech. The investigation into Tegwen Devichand's actions is ongoing.

A campaign group founded by relatives of British troops killed in Iraq aims to use crowdfunded legal action to pursue individuals responsible for the 2003 Iraq War, as the Chilcot report finds IRAQ WAR FAMILIES CAMPAIGN GROUP SEEKS LEGAL ACTION AGAINST THOSE INVOLVED IN THE 2003 IRAQ WAR, CHILCOT REPORT FINDS UK TROOPS WERE SENT INTO BATTLE ill-prepared and that the legal basis for military action was rejected, while the former Prime Minister, Tony Blair, has apologized for any mistakes made, but not the decision to go to war itself. The group seeks guidance from lawyers on the possibility of successful legal action against key individuals involved in the Iraq War. Estimates vary on the number of Iraqi civilians killed over the period.

Adnan Syed's legal team is reopening his case for the 1999 murder of Hae Min Lee, after new evidence from the Serial podcast regarding mobile phone records and a potential alibi has been allowed by a judge. Asia McClain, a friend who claims to have seen Syed at a library during the time of the suspected crime, could serve as his alibi. The defense team will also challenge the prosecution's reliance on mobile phone records, claiming they were misleading and improperly admitted at trial.

A 16-year-old boy, who previously served custodial sentences for assaults at younger ages, admitted assault and theft at a Dundee party after pulling a machete on a taxi driver, prompting another boy to steal the driver's change. The court deferred sentence until next month for a social work background report.

John Clancy, a Labour councillor for Quinton, was elected as the new leader of Birmingham City Council after five attempts, beating closest rival Penny Holbrook in a ballot by a single vote. Clancy aims to improve social housing, make smarter financial decisions, provide free school meals for all primary-age children, and expand regeneration outside the city centre, while facing ongoing government scrutiny due to the Trojan Horse inquiry.

In interviews with Empire magazine in June, Sir Roger Moore and producer Barbara Broccoli discussed their approaches to playing James Bond and how Sean Connery's unconventional portrayal of the character shattered traditional ideas of a movie leading man. Empire magazine also highlighted unsung heroes involved in Connery's performance, such as a dance teacher and a tailor.

Witches' marks, carvings believed to provide protection against witches and evil spirits during the medieval era, have been found in various historical structures such as Shakespeare's birthplace and Tower of London, and Historic England aims to encourage documenting these symbols during Halloween, as significant records about their occurrence and types are scarce.

The article describes an unusual moment during Prime Minister's Questions when Jeremy Corbyn compared Theresa May's lack of a clear Brexit plan to the character Baldrick from Blackadder, played by Sir Tony Robinson, a Labour member, who has been critical of Jeremy Corbyn's leadership. The prime minister took the comparison in stride, pointing out Sir Tony's political affiliation, and the event sparked a flurry of social media activity from the actor.

The Liverpool County Court has ruled that airlines in the UK should pay compensation to passengers for delays in flights, overturning applications by Jet2, Thomas Cook, Ryanair, and WizzAir to delay payments, setting a precedent for thousands of similar claims in the UK.

Jamie Dimon, CEO of JP Morgan, warns that the control of job migration post-Brexit is no longer in the UK's hands as the EU dictates movement of jobs out of London, with France offering incentives like lower taxes, English law courts, and English-speaking schools to attract bankers, with HSBC's CEO also expressing interest despite historical French hostility towards finance.

China has reportedly deployed anti-aircraft missiles on a disputed island in the South China Sea, which it claims is for self-defense under international law. The U.S. is expressing concern about the issue and expects to have a serious conversation with China regarding it. Various nations, including China, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia, and Brunei, claim territory in the resource-rich region, leading to tensions and concerns about the potential militarization of the area.

The study reveals that Adanson's house spider uses its silk draglines to stabilize its body and brake during a jump, allowing it to land poised for prey capture. This adjustable silk tension could inspire the design of future miniature robots capable of such agile movements.

The Supreme Court ruled that UK ministers are not legally obligated to consult devolved legislatures, including Wales, on the triggering of Article 50, but the ruling leaves open the possibility for the Welsh Assembly to have a vote on the issue, with no veto power, and potentially influencing the UK government to respect the Sewel Convention for the matter. All sides agree that the assembly does not have a veto power over Brexit.

The Co-op Bank, known for its ethical stance and having four million customers, has announced that its recapitalization plan with existing investors is substantially agreed, aiming to alleviate its financial struggles and satisfy Bank of England regulations, despite still carrying a share of the Co-operative Group's £8bn pension liabilities.

The Swansea tidal lagoon project is causing a dispute between Tidal Lagoon Power and Natural Resources Wales over fish mortality claims, with TLP disputing NRW's figures and NRW maintaining that its calculations are based on the best available evidence. Both the Welsh Government and UK government ministers are considering the findings of a review of the project's viability.

The article humorously recounts the most notable humorous and sexist mistakes from a reality business competition show, highlighting unexpectedly outdated choices, sexist question choices, navigation mishaps, and dreadful presentations by the contestants, offering viewers the satisfaction of feeling amused by the contestants' missteps.

The Home Affairs Select Committee found that the UK's immigration cap, which limits recruitment from outside the EU, has been counter-productive, as it has stimulated recruitment from EU countries, led to the rejection of nursing job applications from non-EU countries, and had the potential to cause a crisis in the NHS during the winter of 2014 due to the prioritization of higher-paid jobs.

Matthew Boyd, a 20-year-old off-duty soldier who served with the Royal Gibraltar Regiment, was punched, beaten, and left unconscious during a night out in Brecon by Jake Vallely, who was on a seven-hour drinking binge. Aaeron Evans, Vallely's friend, was cleared of manslaughter as he was not present during the attack. Vallely will be sentenced on 8 December, while the community of Brecon is encouraged to avoid conflicts and violence during night outs. Pte Boyd, who was originally from Carrickfergus, County Antrim, was described as an "all-rounder" by his family with a promising career ahead.

The BBC, in collaboration with This Place, has developed a brainwave-reading headset that allows users to control the iPlayer on-demand platform, potentially providing assistance to those with disabilities and contributing to the growing trend of manipulating electronic devices using brainwaves.

The chief inspector of schools, Meilyr Rowlands, stated before the Welsh Assembly's Children, Young People and Education Committee that the current education system's focus on performance measures encourages schools to prioritize borderline C and D grades in GCSEs and may not adequately support more able learners, stifling their progress. The Welsh Government recognizes this issue and is introducing changes to raise standards and extend opportunities for all young people, particularly the most able, through programs such as the Seren Network.

The unreleased 1981 and 1984 recordings by Johnny Cash, featuring duets with his wife June Carter and friend Waylon Jennings, titled "Out Among the Stars", will be released in March, posthumously. The recordings, featuring 12 tracks, were found gathering dust in a vault in 2012 and have never been made public before. Carter Cash maintains the release is worthwhile for fans and compares it to discovering an unseen Picasso, given Cash's immense success (over 90 million records sold) and his history of reaching out to underrepresented audiences.

The tribunal ruled that Maria McKeith was unfairly dismissed from her part-time role at the Ardoyne Association for being a primary carer of a disabled daughter, which contradicts the Disability Discrimination Act 1995. The court of appeal dismissed the Ardoyne Association's appeal. McKeith was awarded compensation of £10,000 for injury to feelings, £6,760 for loss of earnings, and £2,126 in interest. Employers are reminded to recognize their obligations under the Disability Discrimination Act, particularly in regard to treating disabled individuals and their primary carers with dignity and respect.

Scottish midfielder Dorrans signs for Rangers, joining the likes of Bruno Alves, Daniel Candeias, Carlos Pena, Eduardo Herrera, Dalcio, Ryan Jack, Alfredo Morelos, and Fabio Cardoso, following two rejected bids by Norwich City. He expressed excitement to begin his journey at Ibrox.

Team Brewster clinched the men's spot for the European Championships by defeating David Murdoch's Olympic silver medallist team 7-2 9-5, while sister Eve Muirhead's rink secured the women's place in a five-game series. Both Muirhead siblings, skip and third respectively, express excitement about competing in a home event, with new coach Glenn Howard providing valuable input. Graham Muirhead's long-term girlfriend, Anna Sloan (third for Team Muirhead), is set to make her return from injury this week.

Following concerns from residents over the composition of beach recharge material for a future project, councillor Pierre Oxley has called a scrutiny meeting for next Tuesday to discuss the issue. Councillor Oxley has accused project leader Peter Halliday of unclear communication regarding the percentage of sand and shingle in the beach recharge, while Halliday has insisted that the council has been transparent throughout the process. The meeting aims to clarify the proportion of beach materials to ensure that recreational needs of residents are met.

John Nelms announced a land use application will be submitted for land in Camperdown Park, partly due to financial issues: an operating loss of £530,000, increased wages, and higher maintenance costs for the aging stadium, despite investments exceeding £200,000. The plan is to enhance Dundee Football Club with a land use application near the city's Ice Arena.

Chris Froome of Team Sky trails overall leader Alberto Contador by 13 seconds in the Criterium du Dauphine, having finished the second stage eight seconds behind Movistar's Jesus Herrada, who won the race after making a decisive break on the final climb at Chalmazel-Jeansagniere.

The ex-EastEnders star Sian Blake, 43, and her sons, Zachary, 8, and Amon, 4, were found dead in their home on Tuesday, and the case is now being treated as a triple murder inquiry. The police are seeking Arthur Simpson-Kent, the partner of Sian, who has reportedly left the UK and travelled to Ghana. The Met police's handling of the case is being investigated by the IPCC following earlier concerns about Sian's welfare, with significant attempts made to conceal the bodies found in the garden during excavations on Tuesday.

Due to multiple match interruptions, Wimbledon organizers have decided to play tennis matches on the traditional rest day (middle Sunday) for the first time since 2004, with at least eight guaranteed singles' matches to be played on Sunday and further details to be released on Saturday.

Sunderland manager Dick Advocaat, who secured the club's safety from relegation last season, has announced his departure less than a year after taking the job, citing a promise to his wife and choosing to forego any financial settlement. His departure continues a trend set by previous managers Gus Poyet and Paolo di Canio, both of whom arrived to save Sunderland from relegation and left the following season. The club, currently without a win in their first eight league matches of the 2015-16 season, has seen little success under Advocaat, with only one win this season against League Two side Exeter in the League Cup.

Russia anticipates a 0.8% GDP decline next year, due to the combined effects of an oil price slump, Western sanctions primarily aimed at oil and gas industries, banks, arms manufacturers and President Putin's elite, and a weakening economy with declines in the manufacturing, construction, agriculture and service sectors. To support the economy, the government doubles bank deposit guarantees and provides financial aid to the country's largest retail bank, Sberbank, through soft loans and subordinated debt.

Opposition leader Raila Odinga is challenging the 2017 Kenyan presidential election results in court, accusing the electoral authorities of fraud and rigging, while foreign observers describe the election as free and fair; the international community urges calm amid fears of potential violence, and Odinga insists he isn't conceding the fight.

A 60-year-old man dies while scuba diving at Agincourt Reef in Far North Queensland, following two French tourists' deaths due to cardiac arrests while snorkeling on a nearby reef just days prior. The incident occurred on a tour boat with safety equipment, including oxygen and defibrillation equipment.

The UK, Scottish governments, and Dundee City Council have collectively agreed on a 3.7 million-pound contract to continue the Dundee-London Stansted route, operated by Loganair, for two more years. The UK Government's contribution is 50% through the Regional Air Connectivity Fund, while the Scottish government and Dundee City Council put in 1.4 million pounds and 400,000 pounds respectively. The route will offer two return flights daily and one on Sunday.

World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) is launching its video streaming service in China, offering live events, original series, reality shows, and classic matches. Success in China will depend on finding and promoting local stars, and competing with other sports that have already established a presence in the country, such as tennis and basketball. The service will be available through its Chinese partner PPTV, with subscribers required to download an app to access the content.

Three men, including a police officer, are being questioned by West Midlands Police over allegations of conspiring to pervert the course of justice and misconduct in a public office, after providing false and malicious information suggesting a terrorist kidnap plot, which led to the force going on high alert and officers being advised to avoid wearing uniforms.

Ireland defeated Poland 5-1 in a World League quarter-final match, with key contributions from McKee (2 goals), Eugene Magee, and O'Donoghue (2 goals). The victory sets up a semi-final against Wales on Saturday, with the winner advancing to the final and World League 3. Ireland's coach Craig Fulton praised his team's pressure on Poland and the areas they were winning the ball, while Poland's standout player was Mateusz Poltaszewski.

Philip Craig, a 38-year-old man from Leeds, was sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum of 25 years for the murder of Christopher Laskaris, a 24-year-old man with Asperger's Syndrome and bi-polar disorder, in November. Craig exploited Laskaris, supplying him with drugs, and killed him with a single stab wound to the heart. Craig returned to the flat where the body remained to steal more possessions, including a TV, games console, and guitars. Laskaris' family stated that his death had a "devastating impact" and that nothing could ever heal their pain and loss. A second man, Dempsey Pattison, who was also charged with the murder, had his case discharged in February.

The police have closed the reinvestigation into the death of Kester David, a former police informant who was found burned under a bridge in 2010, and apologized for initial failures to properly investigate; the Met Commissioner Sir Bernard Hogan-Howe admitted to a "catalogue of errors" and insensitivity towards David's family, while stating that the reinvestigation was thorough but concluded there was no evidence of a third party involvement in his death.

In 2015, football was the most attended sport in the UK with 43.4 million, followed by three horse racing events in the top 10. Rugby union attendances rose to 7.5 million due to the World Cup. Wimbledon remained the most popular individual event with nearly half a million spectators. Horseracing saw record attendance of 6.2 million, with names like Royal Ascot, Cheltenham Festival, and Epsom Derby in the top tier. Two new events entered the top 10 - MotoGP's British Grand Prix and the Badminton Horse Trials.
