Overall, attendance fell short of the 2012 record, but with a 6% rise without one-off events like the Olympic Games and Rugby World Cup, major sports in 2016 included UCI Track Cycling World Championships, European Aquatics Championships, and FIH Women's Champions Trophy in hockey.

Beyoncé topped the Forbes list of highest-earning music artists, accumulating an estimated $105 million (£66 million) in 2013-2014, with Taylor Swift following closely in second at $64 million (£40 million), Pink at third with $52 million (£32.5 million), Rihanna in fourth with $48 million (£30 million), and Katy Perry at fifth with $40 million (£25 million). The earnings were calculated from touring, record sales, publishing, merchandise sales, endorsements, and other ventures between June 2013 and June 2014, featuring data from organizations such as Nielsen SoundScan. Other notable artists that failed to make the top 10 include Madonna, Nicki Minaj, and Alicia Keys.

The Scottish National Party (SNP) has not been recognized as the official opposition by Speaker John Bercow, despite the party claiming more support among MPs than Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn. The SNP has not been able to fill the shadow Scottish secretary position previously held by Ian Murray, but the ability to fill other relevant shadow positions remains unclear.

Villagers in Crickhowell have successfully launched a bid to buy The Corn Exchange after protests haltered Punch Taverns' plans, with the intention to turn it into independent shops and flats, and preserve their High Street.

Alliance Trust is reviewing its strategy and considering potential actions such as a sale or outsourcing, with a deal with RIT Capital still possible while RIT Capital has declined a formal bid after preliminary discussions about a potential merger, and Alliance Trust is temporarily halting share buybacks.

Alexis Scott, 39, a former Police Community Support Officer, was convicted for tricking passengers in April 2013 into believing they had too much cash when boarding flights, resulting in them giving her money under false pretext. Judge James Mahoney recognized the "persistent, planned, and subtle" nature of her crimes, noting the severe impact on public trust and the international reputation of the country. The victims lost approximately £13,500, which Sussex Police later repaid.

TrueTube and Horrible Histories, along with other productions, have been nominated across multiple categories in the upcoming Bafta Children's Awards, with TrueTube's works being recognized for their impact on young audiences' media consumption patterns. The winners will be announced on 20th November at the Roundhouse in London.

Lady Mary Soames, the last surviving child of Sir Winston Churchill, allocated most of her late father's artwork to the National Trust, Houses of Parliament, and Churchill War Rooms. The paintings include Lady Soames' favorites - Coast Scene near Cannes (1935) and View From a Bathing Hut at the Miami Surf Club, 1946. This selection for the nation includes Churchill's artworks, along with a painting of him standing at his easel, and the Aly Khan Gold Cup, won by his horse, High Hat. These artworks will be displayed in significant locations that influenced Churchill's life, in commemoration of the 50th anniversary of his death.

An ex-investigator from the ombudsman's office was arrested for allegedly stealing sensitive security documents, which police and MI5 believe could endanger lives. The documents don't relate to any current investigation by the ombudsman's office. The police have launched a criminal investigation and have temporarily halted the sharing of sensitive material with the ombudsman's office until a review of security protocols is conducted. Both the Police Federation and Ulster Unionist MP are calling for an independent investigation into the matter due to concerns about the office's integrity.

Phyllis Schlafly, a staunch conservative and outspoken opponent of feminism and abortion, is remembered for her role in blocking the Equal Rights Amendment, her influence on the Republican Party, and her endorsement of Donald Trump, who described her as a patriot and a champion for women after her death. Her legacy also includes her fight against Communism and the founding of the conservative group Eagle Forum.

Professional rugby player Aled Morgan, 23, will leave Bristol at the end of the season, choosing to move back to Wales to further his career development and aim for a place in the Welsh national team. He has attracted interest from several clubs, including Newport Gwent Dragons, and can play at full-back or fly-half. His move to Bristol in 2014 resulted from limited game-time at fly-half for the Ospreys due to competition from Dan Biggar and Sam Davies.

The article reports that Mufawaka Alabash and Asem Alfrhad were found not guilty of causing the death of Alan Kurdi, a three-year-old Syrian refugee whose image lying dead on a Turkish beach focused global attention on the refugee crisis in September 2015, but were convicted of people smuggling. Alan's five-year-old brother Galib and his mother Rihan also drowned during an attempted boat crossing to Greece.

Robert Lady, a former employee of the CIA, returned to the U.S. after serving a nine-year sentence for his involvement in the abduction of Egyptian cleric Abu Omar, known as the first trial involving extraordinary rendition, which has been criticized for violating international agreements. To date, none of the 26 individuals convicted in the case have appeared in an Italian court, with only two having contact with their lawyers.

Scottish airports reported significant increases in passenger numbers for January 2017, with Edinburgh leading the pack at 11.7%, followed by Glasgow at 8.4%, and Aberdeen experiencing its lowest decline in almost two years. Growth in Edinburgh came mainly from international flights, while Glasgow saw an increase in both international and domestic traffic, with strong demand on routes to Toronto, New York, Dubai, and European cities. Aberdeen's decline was attributed to decreased helicopter traffic and inclement weather conditions. Ryanair announced plans to extend its schedule in Aberdeen with new flights to Faro, Riga, and the Faroe Islands.
YouTube has increased the maximum view limit for videos from 2,147,483,647 to 9,223,372,036,854,775,808, after Gangnam Style by Psy surpassed the old limit.

England aim to win against Sri Lanka to secure a place in the World Twenty20 semi-finals for the second time since its inception in 2007. Sri Lanka, who defeated Afghanistan in their opening match, are a formidable opponent due to their quality spinners, although they have lost key players since their peak. England are looking to improve on their previous disappointing performance against the West Indies, West Indies, and Afghanistan.

Scotland's largest cities, Edinburgh and Glasgow, rank second and third respectively in Britain for being the most congested, with estimated losses of £2.8bn and £2.3bn for Edinburgh and Glasgow respectively over the next decade due to traffic jams. According to a study by Inrix Roadway Analytics, the UK-wide total for wasted time in traffic jams is projected to reach £61.8bn by 2025 if congestion levels persist without intervention. In Europe, London is found to have more traffic "pinch points" than any other city and ranks worst in an assessment of the impact of its traffic jams. Researchers suggest identifying traffic hotspots and analyzing their root causes as a key strategy for addressing the issue of congestion.

In a friendly match, Norway scored three unanswered goals against Northern Ireland, with contributions from Elyounoussi, Ruud, and Nordtveit. Northern Ireland had a few goal attempts, but were unable to capitalize.

Authorities in Belgium maintain high alert levels and have charged five people with terrorism offences in connection with the Paris attacks, with Salah Abdeslam still at large and an arrest warrant issued for Mohamed Abrini. Public transport in Brussels is gradually resuming, but some lines remain closed. The leaders of France and the US have pledged to work together to eradicate IS and have called for increased cooperation with France to hit IS targets in Iraq and Syria.

A series of coordinated bombings occurred on March 22 at Zaventem Airport and Maalbeek metro station in Brussels, resulting in 31 deaths and multiple injuries, leading to national mourning and transport disruptions in the city. Suspected links to the 2015 Paris attacks have been raised, and the events are characterized as extremely rare, with public support and memorials pouring in.

Sheffield City Council has served a pre-action protocol letter to local Green Party councillor Alison Teal, threatening a High Court injunction over her ongoing involvement in protests against the city's tree felling program. The city council maintains that the removals are lawful and necessary, but will seek legal action against those engaging in direct action that unlawfully interferes with their works.

In one of the worst whale stranding incidents in New Zealand's history, over 400 whales have stranded themselves at Farewell Spit, South Island, with approximately 300 deaths reported. Local residents and conservation department staff are working together to refloat the survivors, often forming human chains, while scientists continue to investigate the causes of whale stranding events. Farewell Spit, known for its shallow waters, is often cited as a location where the whales mistakenly navigate, leading to many such incidents. New Zealand has one of the highest rates of whale and dolphin strandings worldwide, with around 300 incidents occurring annually.

The Welsh rugby club Ospreys have signed 32-year-old scrummager Brian Mujati as injury cover for Dmitri Arhip and Ma'afu Fia, with Rhodri Jones currently on international duty. Mujati, who has experience playing in Super Rugby, Top 14, and English Premiership, is expected to significantly bolster the team amidst their busy schedule of PRO12 games and a Challenge Cup quarter-final.

The Gwynedd council proceeds to establish a new Church in Wales campus at Ysgol y Berwyn in Bala, despite opposition from 500 community members and concerns about trust from the governors of the schools involved.

The Oxfordshire County Council is proposing a one-council plan to streamline local government and save £100m over five years, while the five district councils are advocating for three councils and an elected mayor for their devolution bid. Residents in the county are being asked for their opinions before the county council's cabinet makes a final decision on March 14th.

Edinburgh rugby team, with Dickinson, Nel, and Ford in the starting front row, must win five tough upcoming matches, starting with Newport Gwent Dragons, to have a chance at a top-six finish. Per Dickinson, they've struggled with errors and soft tries, and have failed to capitalize on opportunities in recent games.

The Northern Ireland Bat Group is rescuing grounded and injured bats that have been found in unusual places due to the poor summer weather conditions, which have affected the bats' mothers' ability to feed and produce milk. Volunteers such as Karen Healy are caring for the bats in their homes, nursing them back to health with a focus on their wing recuperation and flight capacity, before releasing them back into the wild. Healy emphasizes the positive impact bats have on the economy, particularly in agricultural pest control, and debunks common misconceptions about them, such as their blood-drinking or blindness.

The Supreme Court is deliberating on whether to expand limitations on the federal law that prevents gun ownership for individuals convicted of domestic violence, as highlighted by Justice Thomas' recent questioning regarding the potential suspension of constitutional rights due to law violations. This comes following Justice Thomas' previous silence in court, attributed to his belief in private conversations with fellow justices and his preference for not questioning lawyers unless he seeks an answer.

A wildlife holiday company, Responsible Travel, based in Brighton, has decided to drop about six tours involving traditional zoos from their selection of 3,500 trips, after their CEO, Justin Francis, deemed them outdated and inadequate in justifying animal captivity, citing limited successful reintroduction of endangered species to the wild and concerns about animal welfare. The decision was supported by wildlife charity, Born Free Foundation, which expressed concerns about the impact of captivity on animals' behavior. Most of the zoos dropped by Responsible Travel are believed to be located in southeast Asia.

A 40-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of murder after police discovered the body of a primary-school-aged child in Faringdon, England. Police have stepped up their presence in the area as a means of providing reassurance, while local residents expressed shock and sadness following the incident. The investigation remains ongoing.

A suspect is accused of breaching the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measures (TPim) for not contacting a monitoring company and reporting to a police station in January, marking a suspected case of TPim breach. The defendant, one of nine British citizens subject to a TPim, currently faces two charges of breaching Section 23 of a TPim order. The Home Office has not commented on the case. The next hearing is set for July, with a trial date yet to be determined.

Qualcomm, the major supplier of chips for smartphones, has agreed to lower royalty rates on patents in China's mobile phone market, a move that could benefit domestic companies like Xiaomi and Huawei, following a ruling that Qualcomm violated China's anti-monopoly law. This adjustment is expected to increase profit and revenue for Qualcomm, with the company planning to concentrate on supporting its Chinese partners.

In the article, it is detailed that Michelle Mellotte, a former doctor, was found guilty of fraud by abusing her role by taking £10,000 from a patient with Alzheimer's, promising to return it that summer. In 2014, she admitted to fraud and was given a suspended prison sentence, as well as being suspended from the medical register. After a hearing by the Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service, Mellotte was ruled to have put patients at risk and brought the profession into disrepute, leading to her no longer being able to practice as a doctor in the UK.

A nearly complete male skeleton, aged between 30 and 49, was found at the bottom of an embankment near the M54 motorway in Shropshire, UK, around 2-3 years ago. The remains were wearing contemporary clothing and investigators are unable to rule out potential criminal activity, as the cause of death remains undetermined.

The archaeological discovery of a 30m square of megaliths, previously hidden and buried within the Avebury circles, is a "great surprise" and potentially one of the earliest structures on the site, which has the potential to commemorate and monumentalise the ancestral house of the first people who lived in Avebury.

The article discusses an opposition to a parking scheme proposal in Reading by hospital staff and residents, arguing that the implementation of pay and display meters could exacerbate parking pressures around the hospital and university areas, thus presenting challenges for staff, patients, and local residents.

US Navy's Petty Officer Aimee Mejia, in a recent two-car accident in Okinawa, was driving under the influence and crashed into a local woman with a cracked breastbone, and had her liberty curtailed by the US military due to her actions, causing increased resentment among Okinawans who oppose the US military presence. The incident happened on Saturday, and PO Mejia was driving off base. The nature of the second car's passengers or any injuries they may have sustained is not specified in the article.

In a highly successful tri-series, England's Lions, coached by former England captain Andrew Flower, displayed impressive batting performances, with Ben Duckett scoring the ninth-highest List A score ever (220 not out) and Zak Crawley making 171, to comfortably beat Sri Lanka A twice and Pakistan A twice, while Dawid Malan (185) and Sam Billings (175) also excelled. Flower praised the young talent and predicted that the selectors will take note of their performances.

Colombia's peace talks with the FARC rebels, mediated by Cuba and Norway, are resuming on 10 December following the release of three hostages. The discussions will focus on de-escalating the conflict and addressing victim's family concerns, with additional talks scheduled for mid-January. The negotiations, which began in 2012, aim to end a five-decade-long conflict that has claimed over 220,000 lives.

The Save Oxfordshire Children's Centres Campaign led a protest against Oxfordshire County Council's plan to replace 44 existing children's centres with eight to save £8m. Former Prime Minister David Cameron was invited to join the protest, and the PM's office responded by stating there is still scope for savings across local government.

A controversial sandcastle depicting a murder victim in a suggestive manner, entered by Devon and Cornwall Police, won a public competition but received criticism for its poor taste, trivialization of serious issues, and potential sexual stereotyping. The police apologized if it caused offense.

Slade, Leyton Orient's football manager, discusses a proposed shift in the club's structure due to a new owner's takeover, emphasizing his focus on football matters and the need for improved team performance, while noting the learning curve involved for both parties due to the owner's lack of football club experience.

Tyrrell Hatton secured a spot at the USPGA Championship, booked a place at The Open Championship for the fifth time in six years, and earned his largest career payday at the Scottish Open, finishing a shot behind the victorious Swede Alex Noren. He is aware that he has missed the cut at his four previous Opens and his main target at Royal Troon is to make it through to the weekend. He will tee off late on the first day and early on the second day.

The 10-year-old Irish-bred horse Many Clouds, known for his successful races including the Cotswold Chase and the Hennessy Gold Cup, suffered a severe pulmonary haemorrhage and collapsed after a race despite having no significant underlying health issues. The racing authorities believe that the haemorrhage is not a common incident in horse racing, and are seeking to understand its causes and potential prevention strategies.

A woman testified in Sheffield Crown Court that she was 12 when she was picked up from a children's home, abused, and taken to Blackpool where she was raped and forced to work in a restaurant, all of which is alleged to have been orchestrated by Basharat Hussain, who along with six others is on trial for child abuse in Rotherham. Hussain denies the claims and his attorney cross-examined the witness, confirming that she had indeed met Hussain. The trial is ongoing.

A 32-year-old racer, Franck Petricola, tragically lost his life after making his comeback at the TT following a serious accident at the North West 200 in 2014. The racing community expresses deep sympathy for his family and friends following the incident, and an investigation is underway regarding the circumstances leading to his death.
The Isle of Man TT will continue despite Guy Martin's absence due to his crash in June, with Peter Hickman, Michael Dunlop, and Dean Harrison expected to deliver exciting performances.

Louisiana is facing a severe flooding emergency in which over 20,000 people have had to be rescued from their homes or cars after torrential rain, with many still trapped. President Barack Obama has declared the state a disaster area, making federal aid available. The floods have caused extensive damage in the worst-affected areas, including the Louisiana capital Baton Rouge, and have been referred to as a "flood of epic proportions" comparable to the disaster caused by Hurricane Katrina in 2005.

US Soccer has agreed to a lawsuit filed by parents on behalf of young soccer players in 2014, and has resolved to limit the amount of heading in practice for children aged 11 to 13, modify substitution rules in relation to concussions, and introduce new safety measures for players that are part of US Soccer's youth national teams and development academy. The Football Association in England is also working on new guidelines regarding head injuries and their long-term effects on the brain.

Former president Nicolas Sarkozy was not aware of the falsification of 11 million euros worth of invoices during his 2012 campaign, according to a deputy director of his campaign, Jerome Lavrilleux. This comes amid investigation of possible fraud and corruption in the UMP party, which could have negative impact on Sarkozy's potential re-election bid in 2017.

The Council of Mortgage Lenders (CML) reported a decrease in home repossessions in the second quarter of a specified year, with fewer than 3,000 homes repossessed compared to the previous quarter and the same period last year. Low interest rates are thought to be contributing to the trend, but the CML cautions borrowers to be prepared for future rate increases. Additionally, there has been a decrease in owner arrears and an increase in tenant evictions by landlords, but specific reasons for these trends are not provided.

Coventry City Council accepted 105 Syrian refugees from October 2018 to the present as part of the UK Government's expanded resettlement program, with costs covered by the Government. Some critics, such as UKIP MEP James Carver, argue that the distribution of refugees across areas in the UK is uneven and Coventry is accepting more refugees than other councils.

Brazil's president, Ms. Rousseff, expresses confidence in hosting a safe and successful Olympic Games in 2016, with the torch relay set to pass through multiple cities, including the Federal District and 26 states, during 90 to 100 days before reaching Rio's Maracana stadium. Despite concerns about delays, security, and water pollution, Ms. Rousseff promises to address these challenges and deliver a historic Olympic event, making Rio de Janeiro the first South American city to host the Olympics.

Irish actress Saoirse Ronan has been nominated for a Golden Globe award for her role in "Lady Bird", making her the youngest actress in seven years to receive a nomination in the Best Actress in a Motion Picture-Musical or Comedy category.

The 20-year-old Ajax player Abdelhak Nouri suffered severe brain damage due to a lack of oxygen supply during a game, as revealed by new tests, with chances of recovery being nil, according to the club statement.

Swansea earned a crucial victory after falling behind against Aston Villa, with Gylfi Sigurdsson's free-kick and Andre Ayew's late goal turning the match around. The win, while difficult after a six-game winless streak, enhances team morale and provides confidence ahead of the upcoming game against Arsenal.

Mani Dad, a boy living with his Polish mother Leyla Dad in Kielce, Poland, is believed to be with his British father Zayn Dean in the UK. Leyla launching family court proceedings, has asked Costa coffee shops customers to look out for Mani and his father, as they are believed to be frequent visitors.

U.S. authorities have changed travel rules for individuals with dual citizenship, including Iranian citizens, under a visa waiver program, causing confusion and preventing travel for individuals like BBC Persian presenter Rana Rahimpour.

Sky is addressing capacity issues at telephone exchanges in areas with the highest impact, causing slower internet speeds for some subscribers, particularly in Doncaster, North Wales, and Bristol. A postcode checking facility has been provided online for users to check if their local exchange has been flagged as having an issue, and Sky reports that less than 5% of its broadband customer base use the affected exchanges.

A Liverpool-based gang, led by Joseph McHale, Kevin Schruyers, and Robin Vaughan, were convicted of targeting ATMs in various locations in Scotland between August and November 2013. The gang used explosives to gain access to the ATMs' safes, and were found guilty of blowing up ATMs, stealing cash, and attempting burglaries in multiple cities. Additionally, they were found to have duped a Scottish local into providing them with a hideaway. Sentencing was deferred until next month at the High Court at Livingston, with police commending the work of officers involved in the investigation and appreciating the public's assistance.

The Scottish Prison Service is taking steps to implement technology that interferes with mobile phone signals at HMP Shotts and HMP Glenochil, aiming to prevent the use of contraband mobile phones by prisoners, following legislation allowing such interference, with the goal of reducing associated criminal activities like drug supply, organized crime, and harassment.

Commemorations were held in several locations to mark 70 years since the Allied liberation of Nazi camps, including Natzweiler-Struthof in Alsace, Bergen-Belsen in Germany, and Jasenovac in Croatia, with notable inmates including French resistance fighters, Jews, and gypsies at each. The events coincided with growing social tensions in France following deadly Islamist shootings. Former French President Francois Hollande participates in the Natzweiler-Struthof ceremony, saying "The worst can always happen, we prevent it by knowing." The President of the World Jewish Congress, Ronald Lauder, attended the Bergen-Belsen ceremony and remembered the image of bulldozers pushing naked bodies into open pits. A ceremony at Jasenovac marked the 70th anniversary of an escape attempt by about 600 inmates, where 80-90 inmates survived.

Actor Johnny Depp and his wife Amber Heard have filed for divorce, citing irreconcilable differences. The split comes amid ongoing legal consequences from an incident involving Heard bringing two dogs into Australia illegally, potentially leading to a public dispute between Heard and Deputy Prime Minister Barnaby Joyce.

The Maersk Tigris, a Marshall Islands-flagged ship with 24 crew members still aboard, remains anchored off Bandar Abbas, Iran, following its seizure by Iranian authorities, reportedly over a court order related to a complaint from a private Iranian company about debts. The ship was carrying commercial goods, but no military equipment, at the time of the seizure and a distress call from the ship was picked up by the US Navy, prompting them to monitor the situation.

The article summarizes that Sarah Pollock, the sister of Seren Bernard who took her own life in foster care in Pembrokeshire in 2012, is still not able to access the full serious case review report due to legal restrictions, despite a fresh call and it being a matter of public interest. The report indicates that Seren had made a previous suicide attempt and further attempts were a possibility, but her mood had lifted in the days prior to her death. Nevertheless, Ms. Pollock feels traumatized and dysfunctional due to unanswered questions, and is continuing to campaign for access to the full report.

Leigh dominated their Super League match against Salford, leading 18-0 at half-time. Despite a drop-goal from Josh Drinkwater, Salford struggled to overcome Leigh's strong defensive effort, ultimately losing 18-7. The victory puts Leigh in a strong position as they prepare for the upcoming playoffs.

Paul Allen, a tech tycoon, is planning to develop a massive aircraft named Stratolaunch Systems, along with partner Burt Rutan, to launch rockets from high altitudes rather than from traditional launch pads. The aircraft, powered by six 747 jumbo jet engines and featuring a wingspan of 385ft, aims to offer cargo transportation for commercial satellite industries and the International Space Station. Initial test flights are scheduled for 2016 following a decade of preliminary design. The booster rocket to be carried will be built by a company owned by Elon Musk, while other tech moguls like Jeff Bezos and Richard Brandon are also involved in private space ventures. The initiative offers more launch flexibility and minimizes weather constraints, developers said.
Derbyshire aim to chase Lancashire's 365-run total, with Alex Davies scoring 89 runs to leave Derbyshire on 27-2 by the end of the day's play.

In the last show of his tenure on "The Daily Show," host Jon Stewart was joined by celebrities like Bruce Springsteen, received messages from John Kerry and John McCain, expressed gratitude to colleagues, fans, and family, and mentioned the show's influence in shaping American political discourse; the show has also contributed to the careers of comedians like Steve Carell, John Oliver, and Stephen Colbert, with #JonVoyage trending on Twitter as a symbolic farewell.

In the article, it is mentioned that Forest, a four-time cup winner and two-time European Cup winner, will begin their quest in the cup competition to secure a spot in the Europa League, starting at Doncaster on Tuesday, while their goalkeeper Dorus de Vries is expected to recover from an injury in a few weeks.

The Arches nightclub in Glasgow, known for its cultural contribution, went into administration due to a 50% revenue loss after authorities imposed a midnight closing time due to drug abuse and disorder, putting 130 jobs at risk. The Scottish Government is working with partners to explore options for its future, and has offered immediate financial support to maintain the current arts program. Ms. White urged a roundtable discussion between Glasgow City Council, Police Scotland, and the Arches' management to potentially reverse the closure or find a solution for reopening. Additionally, staff affected would be supported through the Partnership Action for Continuing Employment (PACE) initiative.

A senior Provisional IRA member, Ivor Bell, was arrested and charged in connection with the 1972 disappearance and murder of Jean McConville, one of the "Disappeared" during the Troubles in Northern Ireland. The Disappeared were individuals abducted, murdered, and secretly buried by republicans during this period, with only nine bodies found to date. McConville, a mother of 10, was wrongfully accused of being an informer, and her body was only recovered in 2003.

Wigan Warriors overcame a 12-men disadvantage after Ben Flower's red card, scoring 21 unanswered points to secure a victory, setting them on a path towards a potential home semi-final in the Super League. The outcome, if maintained, would also guarantee a place in the final for a fourth consecutive season. Warrington, however, only need a draw to win the first piece of Super League silverware this season.

In September, the poppy arch installation, Wave, at Yorkshire Sculpture Park drew a remarkable 170% increase in visitors, with approximately 100,000 people, compared to around 37,000 last year. This nationwide tour of poppies from the artwork Blood Swept Lands and Seas of Red, which commemorated 100 years since the start of World War One, promises the park's biggest year ever, with over half a million visitors. The sculpture is reported to offer a unique, "calm and contemplative" experience for many visitors.

A severe flood warning on the A361 between East Lyng and Burrowbridge was lifted on 10 March after inspection and clearance work. Temporary traffic lights remain, and the A372 will remain closed for flood pump removal next week. Councillor Harvey Siggs expressed appreciation for efforts to reopen the A361, urging motorists to proceed with caution due to water-filled rhynes along the road.

The Subaru telescope's observation reveals a new icy body, V774104, approximately 15.5 billion km from the Sun, making it the farthest known object in the Solar System. The team led by Scott Sheppard and Chad Trujillo, who specialize in detecting Solar System outliers, announced the discovery at the 47th annual meeting of the American Astronomical Society's Division for Planetary Sciences. V774104 is around 500-1,000 km across, and its orbit needs to be studied further to determine its shape and extent.

Ashley Yates, a headteacher at The Tynings Primary School in Staple Hill, admitted to making indecent images of children and voyeurism, using a spy pen to record pupils and staff. Police have identified additional adult victims, offering support to them. Yates remains in custody, with the next court hearing scheduled for August 9th.

The article summarizes the victory of Helen Glover and Heather Stanning in the women's pairs rowing event at the Rio Olympics, where they defended their Olympic title from the London Games in 2012. They finished 1.2 seconds ahead of New Zealand and broke the record of being unbeaten in 39 races over five years. The duo's success was met with praise from former Olympic rower Sir Steve Redgrave and others on social media.

Steve from Deadly 60, who currently appears on Strictly Come Dancing, expressed concern about the casual use of the term "bullying" and stated he has not used it. In response to recent allegations that he and partner Ola were being bullied, Steve shared that his biggest learning experience on the show has been dealing with the situation, and his approach was to maintain a united front with Ola while addressing the issue truthfully. Steve and Ola were eliminated from this week's competition.

Inflation dropped to 2.6% in June, causing the British pound to initially fall against the dollar and euro and boost the FTSE 100 due to the weaker pound strengthening the value of overseas earnings of multinational companies in the index, and also causing a rise in Royal Mail shares due to increased revenues.

Actress Vicky McClure, who has a tram named after her in her hometown Nottingham, shared a humorous anecdote on The Graham Norton Show about an incident in 2015 where she and her mother were mistakenly accused of fare evasion despite receiving a free ride offer after the tram's unveiling ceremony. Despite the confusion, McClure opted to keep her name on the tram.

The inquest into the death of 14-year-old Alice Gross in the River Brent, west London in 2014, will examine if government and police failures contributed to her death and investigate why Latvian murder convict Arnis Zalkalns, the prime suspect in Alice's death, was allowed to live unchecked in the UK. Alice's family is seeking to establish the robustness of systems for monitoring foreign offenders and cross-border information sharing, expressing dismay over the lack of monitoring of Zalkalns, and urging measures to prevent such incidents from reoccurring.

The Local Data Company and University of Stirling's joint study shows a drop in Scotland's retail vacancy rate from 14.5% to 13.7%, with East Kilbride (33%) and Inverurie (1%) leading and lagging respectively, and 40% of empty shops vacant for over three years. Improved towns include Anstruther, Clydebank, Dumfries, Inverkeithing, Lochgelly, Peterhead, and Pitlochry, while Dundee, Banff, Dumbarton, Cumbernauld, East Kilbride, and Ardrossan have the highest rates. Leisure businesses are increasingly significant, with over 30% of shops being leisure in certain areas. The study suggests that over 40% of empty units have been vacant for over three years, which may indicate a barrier to healthy and sustainable communities.

Rory McWhirter, a Scottish man from Edinburgh, was sentenced to prison for a sophisticated fraud scheme where he deceived individuals into applying for fake jobs, obtained their marriage certificates, registered fake births using the certificates, claimed over £34,000 in benefits under false identities, and was found guilty of fraud. Despite his attorney's argument that McWhirter would be able to repay the money if not jailed, the scheme was deemed to be a significant attack on the public purse and the integrity of the system of births, deaths, and marriages, as well as the system of working tax credits, child benefit, and maternity grants, thus warranting imprisonment.

Authorities are attempting to demolish Awamiya's old quarter, a predominantly Shia area, citing it as a militant hideout, but activists allege security forces are forcibly displacing residents. The unrest escalated with at least seven fatalities, including police officers, in clashes, according to Reuters. Local activists claim indiscriminate shooting and property damage, while water scarcity threatens the town's citizens. The UN has criticized the demolition, with power cuts allegedly used as a means to force people out, particularly in the 400-year-old al-Masora quarter, home to 2,000–3,000 residents. The region has a history of discrimination and marginalization, as well as protests and attacks, dating back to the 2011 Arab Spring uprisings and exacerbated by the 2016 execution of Shia cleric Nimr al-Nimr, a resident of Awamiya.

Young people in Belfast express frustration over lack of job opportunities and feel let down by the political system, which they believe is too focused on personal gain and not doing enough to skills-train the workforce or foster positive social changes such as drug reform and better healthcare.

A Barnet council chief executive, Andrew Travers, left his role after a registration issue occurred during the EU referendum in June 2016, prompting a review of the electoral process to ensure future fairness.

Manager Neil Warnock has provided midfielder Peter Whittingham time to consider a new contract offer, stressing that respect is due to the veteran player who recently celebrated ten years at the club, while making it clear that Emyr Huws and Stuart O'Keefe are not part of his long-term plans.

The BBC and BuzzFeed News investigation revealed suspected match-fixing in elite tennis, with a tennis representative stating that if found guilty, players should be banned permanently, emphasizing the importance of maintaining the sport's purity and fairness. The Scottish tennis player, Fleming, expressed surprise about the issue at higher levels, suggesting additional funding for the Tennis Integrity Unit to address it. He assured viewers that the Australian Open is free of such activities.

A 60-year-old man, reportedly a local customer, entered a bank in Northfield, pulled out a firearm, and held a female staff member hostage for approximately an hour before surrendering to police. He was taken to the hospital for an assessment and is expected to be questioned for firearms offenses. The incident did not result in any injuries to customers or staff members.

Mohammed Ali, a computer software programmer from Liverpool, is on trial for allegedly attempting to illegally possess the toxic substance ricin after being deceived by undercover FBI agents on the dark net. Ali is accused of trying to purchase 500mg of ricin, which is enough to kill many people, mimicking a character from the TV series "Breaking Bad." The trial is ongoing.

Newport County AFC, tenants of Rodney Parade along with rugby teams Newport Gwent Dragons and Newport RFC, are facing criticism from an opposing team's manager regarding the condition of the pitch at the stadium. The CEO of Rodney Parade Limited, Ian Davies, acknowledges the issue, explaining that there is no short-term solution and that the high costs of proposed drainage work are a concern.

The Aviva UK Health report reveals that a significant majority (69%) of those surveyed have worked while unwell, fearing a backlog of work upon their return, while only 23% admitted to faking sickness. This is after official figures show a record low in sick days taken, with UK workers labeled as "mucus troopers." The report suggests that businesses should create working cultures that allow for proper sick leave management to reduce overall business performance losses due to presenteeism.

The Bank of England kept interest rates unchanged and adjusted its 2017 growth forecast downward, while the FTSE 100 remained almost flat with positive contributions from mining stocks; but Fresnillo, Randgold Resources, and Antofagasta rallied, while Hikma plummeted due to a delayed US approval for a new drug and Centrica, BT, and Mondi suffered losses due to regulatory concerns, dividend payouts, and lower profits.

Russian hacker Roman Seleznev was found guilty of running a hacking scheme from 2008 to 2014 that targeted US pizza chains in Washington state, stealing and selling nearly 3 million credit card numbers. He will be sentenced on December 2 and faces a mandatory minimum jail term of four years. His lawyers plan to appeal the conviction, alleging illegal arrest and the use of corrupted evidence and claiming that the case was politically motivated. Russia has lodged official complaints about Seleznev's seizure and extradition.

The article states that in response to questions about alleged tapes of his conversations with former FBI Director James Comey, President Trump claimed on Twitter that he does not have any such recordings. This claim comes after Comey confirmed that Trump had requested Flynn investigation be dropped and asked for loyalty, and following reports of a private meeting where Trump had asked Comey to let go of an investigation into Mike Flynn.

Tata Steel assets are being bid upon by Liberty, led by Sanjeev Gupta, with potential financial backing from Macquarie Bank and a team of advisers. A separate management buyout team, Excalibur Steel UK Limited, is also planning to submit a bid. Tata Steel has not publicly set a deadline for any deal, but has made it clear it cannot sustain its financial losses indefinitely. The UK government has offered support for a potential buyer, including a stake and substantial financing.

Local councils in the East Midlands region are considering a proposal to extend the Nottingham tram service to East Midlands Airport and the proposed HS2 station at Toton as part of their broader "priority projects" in devolution negotiations. The Light Rail Transit Association supports this idea, claiming it would efficiently move passengers from the HS2 station to cities like Derby and Nottingham, following a trend of modern tramway development in France and the continued success of trams in Germany. The costs and timetable of the project were not discussed in the document.

Ronnie O'Sullivan, world number six and five-time world champion, attributed his 10-1 win at the Masters to modifying his game to remain competitive with younger players, such as Neil Robertson, Judd Trump, and Ding Junhui. Despite taking up smoking during the tournament and feeling unwell, O'Sullivan stated that winning the Masters boosted his self-belief and gave him confidence going into the World Championship in April, where he will seek a sixth title. He added that it was "unbelievable" to equal Stephen Hendry's record for most Masters wins.

A devastating storm swept across Poland, killing six people, damaging thousands of homes, and devastating over 45,000 hectares of forest, with particularly heavy damage in Torun, Gdansk, and Poznan. The disaster is being called the worst forestry disaster in Poland and potentially all of Europe. The storm comes after the Polish government has faced criticism for logging in the Bialowieza forest, a Unesco World Heritage site and home to rare wildlife, with the European Union's court ordered the immediate stopping of large-scale logging operations last month.

Singer Enrique Iglesias had to undergo additional reconstructive surgery after injuring his hand while attempting to grab a drone camera at a concert, and is expected to take several weeks to recover before resuming his tour on July 3 in Mexico City.

Leeds Rhinos defeated Warrington Wolves 32-0, with Matt Parcell scoring three tries and Rob Burrow making a significant impact on the game. Warrington, who have struggled with execution and ball handling, were nilled in the match. Leeds' coach Brian McDermott felt his team was clinical, but did not comment on Warrington's specific performance issues.

William (Plum) Smith, a central figure in the 1994 ceasefire of loyalist paramilitary groups, spent ten years in prison for a 1972 shooting incident. After his release, he became a member of the Progressive Unionist Party (PUP), served as its chairman, and played a crucial role in negotiating the UVF and Red Hand Commando into the peace process, stemming from his leadership in arranging the 1994 Combined Loyalist Military Command ceasefire. Known for his intelligence and compassion, Smith's contributions to peace were recognized by Deputy First Minister Martin McGuinness and others in the public sphere.

Mrs. Olive Cooke, a 92-year-old resident of Bristol, has been a dedicated poppy collector for the Royal British Legion for over 75 years, selling poppies at Bristol Cathedral's entrance for the past 12 years. Her dedication stems from the loss of her first husband, Leslie Hussey-Yeo, in 1943 during World War II and a deep appreciation for the sacrifices made by young men during both world wars, many of whom were her school friends. The RBL appreciates her as their "most-valued poppy collector."

Shimon Peres, a key Israeli statesman present at the nation's birth in 1948, who served as prime minister twice and president, won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1994 for his role in the Oslo Accords, passed away in a Tel Aviv hospital following a major stroke two weeks earlier. His legacy includes arms purchasing for the IDF, the Entebbe rescue operation, shifting towards political doveishness regarding Palestinian territories, and advocating for peace.

A BBC report reveals that 70% of Queen's University staff took part in a survey, with only about 29% agreeing that senior leaders provided effective leadership and just over one in five saying the university managed change effectively. However, the circumstances were more positive about other aspects of the university, including its reputation in Northern Ireland, research commitment, and interesting work. The university has pledged to work with staff in response to the survey results and address identified challenges.

The X-47B, a tailless, jet-powered unmanned aircraft being developed by Northrop Grumman for the US Navy, successfully undertook its maiden flight, showcasing its potential as a stealthier, faster, and more advanced member of the future generation of drones, designed to eventually perform tests from an aircraft carrier in 2013.

Airbus has reduced the production of double-decker A380 aircraft due to decreased demand and faces potential A350 cancellation from Qatar Airways due to Pratt & Whitney engine problems, while also experiencing delays in A320neo aircraft deliveries.

The article reports that 40% of coral in the Dongsha Atoll in the South China Sea has died due to a spike in water temperatures up to 6 degrees Celsius, caused by a high-pressure system. Experts suggest that current predictions about the future of coral reefs, including a 2-degree Celsius cap on ocean warming, may be overly optimistic for shallower reefs like Dongsha, as a minor local weather shift can amplify the warming impact.

Scientists have discovered a proteinHi1afound in Australian funnel-web spider venom that shows great promise as a potential future stroke treatment, as it blocks acid-sensing ion channels in the brain. However, the research is still in its early stages, and the protein's effectiveness and safety in human trials remain to be confirmed.

The article describes a football match between Oldham Athletic and Bradford City, where Oldham scored first through a header by Peter Clarke from a free-kick, but Bradford dominated possession and equalized through a penalty kick converted by Billy Clarke after a foul by Ousmane Fane. Despite numerous chances on both sides, the game ended in a 1-1 draw.

The article reports that the experimental drug, aducanumab, has shown to be safe and may potentially halt memory decline by reducing amyloid plaques in the brain, although further, larger studies in phase 3 are necessary to fully evaluate its effects on cognitive decline in patients with very early-stage Alzheimer's. Experts are cautiously optimistic, but warn of previous disappointments in Alzheimer's drug development.

In an unexpected outcome, the second-tier Oldham Roughyeds defeated Hull KR of the Super League 28-10, with a 24-6 lead at halftime. The Roughyeds' coach described his team's victory as "probably the biggest win" since the club reformed. Hull KR's coach, on the other hand, described his team's performance as a "biggest embarrassment" of his career. Meanwhile, Leigh and Batley Bulldogs have also advanced to the next round of the Challenge Cup.

In the article discussing plans for the future of the BBC, Tony Hall proposes a "new, open BBC" that emphasizes cooperation with cultural bodies, funding for local reporters to support local journalism, a children's content service, and a platform for understanding the world. The BBC director general warns of funding cuts that could lead to the loss or reduction of some services, without specifying which areas might be affected. These plans have faced criticism from some media organizations who fear the BBC's initiatives could undermine existing local news publications.

The Equality and Human Rights Commission has expressed concern about a rise in hate attacks, including racial, anti-Semitic, and homophobic attacks, following the UK's vote to leave the EU. The commission calls for accurate information and respectful debate from politicians, and criticizes the government's aborted plan to demand companies set out the proportion of foreigners they employ, suggesting there should be a review of hate crime sentences.

In the article, Ms. Evans, who was suspended from UKIP for six months, expressed a desire to run for the party's leadership but was prevented from doing so by a small group of party leaders due to personal reasons. She also endorsed Lisa Duffy as the best candidate to lead UKIP, which she believes needs a clean break from its hard-right image, internal reform, and a shift towards the center-ground to grow and thrive.

The article discusses an upcoming change in England's GCSE system, starting with students turning 13 this academic year, where a new grading system using numbers instead of letters and moving away from coursework will be implemented for English language, English literature, and maths. Other popular GCSE subjects will follow suit the following year, with exams in 2018.

Retired General David Petraeus, who served as CIA director under Presidents Bush and Obama, indicated his willingness to serve under President-elect Trump, considering Trump's personal demeanor as described by those who have met him recently, and firmly advocates for possible improved U.S.-Russia relations, likening the potential opportunity to President Nixon's successful diplomatic overtures to China in the 1970s.

Hillary Clinton met with Egyptian President Mohammed Mursi and urged both parties to compromise to stabilize Egypt's democracy, while also encouraging the military to return to a purely military role and Mursi to protect women's rights and uphold the peace treaty with Israel.

Derek Bruder testified about his 1990 meeting with West Midlands Police Inspector Matthew Sawers concerning the final movements of 15-year-old Kevin Williams during the FA Cup semi-final between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest on April 15, 1989. Bruder originally felt a pulse in Kevin but later changed his statement about pulses after a discussion with a pathologist. Bruder accused Sawers of trying to pressure him to alter his original statement, while Sawers denied any misconduct. The inquest, examining the 96 deaths at the match, will continue on Monday.

The pop duo Oh Wonder found inspiration for their second album, Ultralife, after positively interacting with strangers on a train, during their two-year career, while releasing a song a month on a budget of £200. The album, set for release on July 14, is focused on capturing moments of human connection and resilience.

Chelsea took the lead against Stoke City with a goal from Bertrand Traore on the right wing, but Diouf equalized after a failed clearance by Courtois. The Potters remained fifth in the table, while Chelsea slipped to 10th place. Traore had a mixed game, starting centrally, with his impressive goal offset by some errors, and was replaced by Alexandre Pato after 68 minutes. Chelsea had several players rested for their Champions League match against Paris Saint-Germain.

The article details Nobel Prize-winning research by William C Campbell, Satoshi Omura, and Youyou Tu leading to drugs for malaria, onchocerciasis (river blindness), and lymphatic filariasis (elephantiasis), benefiting 3.4 billion people. Ivermectin, discovered in Japan, targets roundworm parasite larvae while artemisinin, discovered by a Chinese scientist, targets malaria-causing parasites. The quest for new drugs continues due to emerging drug-resistant strains.

The Nelson Mandela Foundation, run by Mandela's colleagues, has criticized South African President Zuma for corruption and named him as the reason democracy is under threat, calling for the African National Congress to take action to remove him from power. Their call comes as a court case begins over a report by former anti-corruption chief Thuli Madonsela who investigates allegations of Zuma's undue influence by the Gupta family, which he denies. Their requested report has been withheld from public release due to Zuma's court action.

Miranda, a comedian and actress, performed her trademark gallop during the curtain call at Annie's opening night at London's Piccadilly Theatre, where her portrayal of Miss Hannigan was praised for being out-of-comfort-zone humorous yet faced mixed reviews. The musical, a tale of an 11-year-old girl's search for her parents set in 1930s New York, received positive responses for its unashamed optimism in light of recent events.

In a home game at St James' Park, Shelvey contributed significantly to Newcastle's 2-1 win over West Ham, with Ayoze Perez and Georginio Wijnaldum scoring the goals. The victory moved Newcastle out of the relegation zone. Despite conceding a goal via a stray backpass from Chancel Mbemba, the home side held on for their first win in six games, with goalkeeper Rob Elliot denying West Ham a late equalizer. Newcastle striker Aleksandar Mitrovic was denied by West Ham's keeper Adrian three times. Both teams have important away matches on January 23, with Newcastle facing Watford and West Ham hosting Manchester City.

Supermarkets Morrisons, Tesco, Asda, and Sainsbury's have reduced diesel prices by up to 2p per litre due to lower wholesale diesel costs and increased diesel production outside of the UK, according to the RAC. These reductions come as a result of strong demand for European gasoline (petrol) from the US and West Africa, which is supporting the wholesale petrol price, creating a surplus of diesel. This diesel surplus is being exported to the US, decreasing demand for petrol in the UK and lowering diesel prices, and potentially resulting in slight reductions in unleaded prices as well. The RAC predicts further price cuts of up to 4p per litre on diesel over the next fortnight.

The ongoing debate about corporal punishment as a disciplinary method for children persists, with the United Nations Committee on the Rights of the Child urging all member states to outlaw it in schools and homes. Some claim that it can cause psychological harm and is a form of abuse.

A warning has been issued by Suffolk Police about a potentially dangerous batch of ecstasy pills containing the highly toxic drug ParaMethoxyMethylAmphetamine (PMMA), which may still be in circulation, following the deaths of four men. These pills have the Superman logo, and PMMA, a potent hallucinogenic stimulant that acts more slowly than MDMA, causes people to overdose as they think it isn't working. Home-testing kits are not effective.

In a letter to Paul Nuttall, UKIP's leader, Darren Grimes urged a return of ex-UKIP leader Nigel Farage, advocated for the hiring of a CEO, and recommended other changes to increase the party's electability, while Nuttall's adviser Patrick O'Flynn disagreed with some of these proposed changes.

The virtual relationship service Invisible Girlfriend, which creates a personalized girlfriend experience through text messaging, has thousands of global subscribers who use it for various reasons, including avoiding unwanted attention, practicing flirting, and seeking companionship, with over 60% of accounts opting for a boyfriend.

Germany displayed their versatile attacking abilities in a 2-0 victory over Poland, featuring key players like Thomas Muller, Karim Bellarabi, and Mario Gotze, but their defense was not immune to occasional errors that could potentially provide opportunities for Scotland in their upcoming match.

Blackburn Rovers and Bristol City draw 1-1, with Tammy Abraham missing chances for City and Sam Gallagher scoring for Rovers late in the game. Rovers face Aston Villa, Brentford, and Wolves in their final games, while City have fixtures against Brighton, Barnsley, and Birmingham remaining.

Scotland aims to send outgoing coach Gregor Townsend on a high by beating Ireland in the opening Six Nations match, as the Scottish players seek inspirational victory to honor their departing coach; the Irish team, having recently defeated heavyweights such as South Africa, Australia, and New Zealand, will employ a focused and tactically sharp strategy, aiming to exploit Scotland's inexperienced front-row.

In the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Kilmarnock, John Guidetti scored a free-kick after Pascali's red card for pulling back Stefan Scepovic. Killie keeper Conor Brennan made several saves, but Scepovic scored a second goal after the break, changing the nature of the match. Celtic overtook Kilmarnock in the standings with the win.

Northern Irish pupils have a similar average satisfaction level with their lives to their counterparts in the UK, but face higher levels of anxiety before exams, bullying, and frequent internet use, according to an international study by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). The study found girls and disadvantaged students were less likely than boys and advantaged students to report high levels of life satisfaction across all participating countries and economies.

In a resilient display, Crystal Palace fought back from behind to defeat Everton 3-2, despite initially struggling against the fresher Everton side. Goals from Mile Jedinak, Fraizer Campbell, and Yannick Bolasie turned the tide in Palace's favour, before Leighton Baines scored a late consolation penalty for Everton.

Gary Carter, a freelance sports journalist who traveled from Manchester to London to report on a rugby league match, was found injured in Bethnal Green early on Friday. He was taken to the Royal London Hospital, where he underwent surgery to remove a blood clot from his brain. A 35-year-old man was charged with causing grievous bodily harm, and a 22-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of affray towards attending paramedics. Members of the sports community, including former footballer Alan Shearer and player Sam Tomkins, expressed their support and well wishes for Carter's recovery.

Tinie Tempah, a seven-time Number One singles-scoring British artist this decade, at his studio where he's been working on his third album, Youth, for over two years, shares that his creative process was influenced by reconnecting with friends from before his success, and he notes the acceptance and success of British rappers like Stormzy and Dave in contemporary music.

Government, Ofcom, and mobile operators are discussing the early allocation of 4G spectrum, with O2 expressing hope for a launch of services in summer 2013 and concerns about delays caused by legal challenges between companies. EE could potentially announce its 4G launch date, but has not yet given a firm date or specific city locations.

The Conservatives are considering ending a policy of providing free school meals for young children in primary school and offering free breakfast instead, potentially leaving some schools with insufficient funds to upgrade kitchens and facing criticisms of the impact on student nutrition and well-being.

A shooting occurred in a busy area of Tel Aviv, wounding four people, three of whom suffered serious injuries. Israeli security forces are searching for the gunman, and it remains unclear if the shooting is a terrorist attack or related to organized crime, as it comes amidst a wave of Palestinian attacks against Israelis in recent months.

Scottish researcher Judi Menabney found the burial location of Dean Owens' great great grandfather Ambrose Salvona, a Victorian lion tamer, in Inverness' Tomnahurich Cemetery, helping Owens discover more about his family history and inspiring the lyrics of his song "Dora" on his album Into the Sea.

The 2023 Glastonbury festival is introducing stainless steel pint cups made from 80% recycled steel. These cups, available exclusively at some main bars, are part of a reusable strategy to reduce single-use plastics. While they are difficult to throw and may not be suitable for urination, they pose less risk to festival-goers than traditional cups when littered. The production of stainless steel does release pollutants, although this is still less harmful compared to the slow degradation of traditional plastic cups in the environment.

A 15-year-old boy was rescued in Kathmandu after surviving the earthquake by drinking water from wet clothes, while a woman was rescued from a collapsed building after eight hours of international rescue efforts. The death toll has risen to over 6,000, with many survivors falling ill due to contaminated water. However, there are concerns about the slow pace of assistance in rural areas.

Major financial institutions, including JP Morgan and Barclays, are considering relocating between 500 and 1,000 jobs from London to cities like Dublin, Frankfurt, and Luxembourg as a contingency plan in anticipation of a hard Brexit that could disrupt passporting rights.

Five-hour curfew imposed in Ferguson, Missouri, after riots and a subsequent shooting in a separate incident, sparked by release of CCTV footage showing Michael Brown, a black teenager, shoplifting in a store. The officer, Darren Wilson, a six-year veteran, has been identified as the shooter, and the US justice department is investigating the shooting.

In the final days of the general election campaign, Diane Abbott, the Labour shadow home secretary, accused Theresa May of allowing police numbers to decline during her tenure as Home Secretary, which Abbott argued had contributed to insufficient safety measures, particularly in the aftermath of terror attacks.

New Zealand defeated Wales 46-6, marking their 29th consecutive loss to New Zealand. Despite the loss, Warren Gatland sees potential for improvement in areas such as counter-attacking, breakdown dominance, and collision acceleration.

Five individuals, including David Thomas, Stephen Thomas, Nigel Hooker, Jack Slater, and Katie Taylor, died in a boat accident onboard the Leviathan II in Tofino, Canada while not wearing life jackets on the open upper deck of the boat. The Canadian government is investigating the cause of the incident, and Jack Slater is being treated in the hospital. Stephen Thomas was a talented photographer and former pupil at Isambard Community School in Swindon. The boat had capsized in the past, killing two individuals. The 27-year-old Australian man on the boat with his girlfriend and her family is still missing.

A deal announced by Myanmar's President Thein Sein aims to resolve long-standing conflicts in the country, but it excludes the largest and most active rebel groups, and concerns remain about the government's adherence to the agreement.

Facebook was ordered by a High Court judge to remove a page about a man with 15 convictions for sexual offenses, who argued it amounted to harassment, privacy invasion, and inappropriate treatment, due to its potentially threatening and harmful content. The judge ruled the interim injunction would cause minimal disruption to Facebook and only requires "modest steps" to ensure the plaintiff is not exposed to further unlawful conduct, without suppressing information about the man's criminal record that is already public.

Publishers must explicitly opt out to avoid being bound by terms for Apple's app service that include indemnifying the tech giant for legal issues involving their RSS content and allowing ads to be placed next to their publicly available content. Some publishers have raised concerns about these terms.

Guam, a US territory with about 165,000 civilians and US military bases, remains a cause for concern among some residents due to North Korean threats, as the small island is considered a potential target for North Korean missiles. Some prefer diplomatic attempts to resolve the situation, while others express a sense of resignation.

The Sentinel-1b spacecraft, carried into orbit by a Soyuz rocket, will work with Sentinel-1a to provide radar imagery for Earth observation applications, including monitoring shipping lanes, icebergs, and land subsidence, among other uses. This is part of the European Union's Copernicus program, which aims to provide diverse Earth observation data, including water management, air quality, and crop monitoring. Other satellites, including the fundamental physics experiment Microscope, were also launched on the same mission.

The pound's 1% gain is influenced by market speculation that Theresa May may gain a larger majority in the snap election, potentially leading to a softer Brexit and benefiting the pound. However, this outcome is not guaranteed and the stock market is down due to the strength of the pound diminishing the value of foreign earnings for UK companies. The election may provide May with more time to negotiate Brexit, but it further complicates an already complex political and economic landscape.

A hiker, Pavlina Pizova, got lost while hiking the Routeburn track in Fiordland National Park and, due to bad conditions, her companion Ondrej Petr slipped and died. After staying with his body for a night, she moved on to find shelter and spent another night out in the open. She then stayed in a hut for nearly a month before being found by a search team. She was later interviewed by police, and Petr's body was recovered and a coroner's inquiry launched.

Russians and millions like Elena are struggling with the burden of personal debt due to years of borrowing, exacerbated by economic downturns, and inadequate regulations that offer little aid in managing or restructuring debts. The article discusses a family's story of getting loans to pay for medical treatment, which spiraled out of control as new expenses arose and credit cards were applied for with unfavorable conditions. With tightened income and few safety nets, many are unable to meet payments, risking bankruptcy and the loss of their homes. The financial ombudsman reports success rates in helping debtors has dropped significantly, leaving many to face the consequences alone.

On July 30, Judge William Sylvester denied an expanded media coverage request for James Holmes, accused of the Aurora movie theater shooting on July 20, which left 12 dead and 58 injured. His court appearance was filmed over objections from his lawyers, and he was found to be dazed and with dyed orange hair. Holmes reportedly has a face guard due to spitting at prison officers, and his apartment was found to contain 30 grenades and several gallons of gasoline rigged as a booby-trap. Meanwhile, Batman star Christian Bale visited victims at a hospital, as officials called for renewed consideration of high-capacity gun magazine bans but faced minimal prospects for success.

The Art Recovery Group, which has recovered over $500 million of stolen and looted art over the past decade, is working to help stop the theft of Syria's precious antiquities by fighting against the unregulated global art market, increasing awareness among collectors and dealers, and using visual recognition software to combat the smuggling of looted objects.

Despite the prediction-worthy magnitude of the 2011 Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant disaster, the commission found major flaws in safety standards and emergency procedures due to systemic issues like ignore societal conventions, regulatory inefficacy, negligence, lack of governance, and inadequate and confusing communication. Moreover, the report revealed that both the operators and regulators neglected their responsibilities, leading to profound public health and welfare issues persisting up to present day.

Small businesses have achieved a high (66%) compliance rate in the latest stage of the government's auto-enrolment programme, which eventually requires offering pensions to employees aged 22 and above who earn more than £10,000 annually. The process targets professionals like nannies and plumbers, with employer contributions averaging 3% of an employee's salary at present. The government is gradually increasing minimum contributions to 8% by 2019; however, concerns persist about ensuring decent retirement standards.

The article summarizes a study led by Tom Gleeson from the University of Victoria, which finds that only 6% of the water stored in the top 2km of Earth's surface, known as modern groundwater, is useful for human consumption or agriculture, and it is quickly renewed but sensitive to climate change and human contamination. The study uses tritium measurements and large data sets on rock and soil permeability, porosity, and water table gradients to determine that this modern groundwater is more evenly distributed globally compared to older groundwater, but unevenly depleted, making it a vital resource that needs sustainable management.

The European Challenge Cup finals will take place in Edinburgh, Scotland in 2017, with both the Challenge Cup and Champions Cup finals being held over the same weekend at a yet-to-be-announced venue, as announced by European Professional Club Rugby. This decision comes as a result of a successful bid supported by the Scottish Government and Event Scotland, as well as Scotland's previous successful hosting of the European Cup finals in 2005 and 2009 at BT Murrayfield.

Edward Snowden, wanted by the US for leaking details of surveillance programs, remains indefinitely at Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport as the delay in processing his temporary asylum application is being sorted out. The White House demanded clarity on Snowden's status, but a final destination for him is uncertain, as reported by Snowden's lawyer.

Brazil's Attorney-General Rodrigo Janot has asked the Supreme Court to investigate former president Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva for his alleged involvement in the Operation Car Wash scandal, which involves a multi-billion dollar kickback scheme at Petrobras. The allegations, related to properties owned by Lula's family, accuse him of receiving illicit benefits, including renovations and donations, from construction firms involved in the scandal. Lula denies any wrongdoing. The exact charges and evidence against Lula are not yet known.

The article summarizes the unfortunate deaths of three SAS candidates, Craig Roberts, James Dunsby, and Edward Maher, during a selection exercise in 2013 due to hyperthermia. Despite a coroner's ruling that neglect contributed to their deaths, the UK government declined to amend the 2007 Corporate Manslaughter Act to hold the Ministry of Defence accountable for training safety lapses. The bereaved families expressed their disappointment with this decision, stating they believed that legal accountability would encourage better safety measures and training methods within the military.

Leicester City, the defending Premier League champions, suffered League One defeat by Millwall in the FA Cup, despite Millwall playing with 10 men for much of the second half. Manager Claudio Ranieri is urging his players to show greater fight to avoid relegation, following a run of poor performances in the league and their inability to win an away game all season. Leicester City have not won an away game in the Premier League since October 2016, and are currently in the relegation zone.

The article discusses HMRC's ongoing investigation into potential tax irregularities related to image rights for 43 footballers, 8 agents, and 12 football clubs, with specific focus on figures like Jose Mourinho and Cristiano Ronaldo, which has yielded £158m in tax recently. The investigation follows the formation of an inter-agency task force and the publication of the Panama Papers and includes a dedicated team at HMRC looking at image rights, football, and the entertainment industry. HMRC has made arrests and has seven criminal investigations underway.

A controversy has sparked in Germany over the investigation of journalists for publishing classified documents revealing expansion plans for online surveillance, igniting a debate about press freedom, government influence, and privacy rights, with government leaders pressured to dismiss the prosecutor.

The Chancellor's recent Budget focused primarily on boosting growth in regional areas, particularly in Greater Manchester and the Midlands, while acknowledging housing as a challenge in the South East, introducing a new ISA to aid first-time buyers, but political opponents criticized the potential widening of the north/south divide due to the lack of mention of the South East in the Budget speech.

A narrow victory was scored by Doncaster Rovers over Colchester United, with Tommy Rowe netting just before half-time in a tight game where Colchester arguably had more dangerous chances throughout the match.

Royal Bank of Scotland's CEO, Ross McEwan, says the uncertainty caused by the upcoming EU referendum might slow down banking in the UK, and a rate hike is unlikely until 2017; he also reaffirmed that the bank is making efforts to recover from past financial missteps, but remains in substantial public ownership and may continue to be so for some time.

At the 2015 general election, the Labour Party opposes a post-election deal with the Scottish National Party (SNP) due to their differences on key issues, and is emphasizing unity, a strong economy, and a welfare state to support the vulnerable. The SNP seeks to establish more progressive policies with a potential minority Labour government. The Liberal Democrats focus on increasing investments in mental health services and positioning themselves in the center ground of politics, while the Conservatives emphasize a robust economy and keeping Scotland within the UK.

A team of students, Elliot Vale and Tia Mountain, have designed an app called GeoRescue, which aims to provide information on natural disasters using advanced maps services and GPS, potentially saving lives. The app, set to present at a space conference in Manchester and be pitched to a Dragons Den-style panel in June, would guide people to safety by emitting a signal using GPS to indicate a person's location for search and rescue services. It is designed to help in the event of a disaster, especially in areas with no internet or signal.

The Scottish government's proposal in the Higher Education Governance Bill to elect the chair of universities' governing bodies, including the chair of the university courts, is criticized by Sir Timothy O'Shea as potentially damaging due to perceived threats to the established role of the rector, potential weaker powers for the senior lay member, and lack of prior consultation, as well as for changing the long-established role of the rector without consultation, and for not consulting on the senior lay member's powers. He also welcomes some amendments to the bill that remove additional ministerial powers that threaten institutional autonomy.

A Ukrainian woman, Elena Hrabovenska, fears potential escalation of hate mail and phone calls towards Polish businesses following the Brexit referendum, and anticipates that the new generation will integrate into the English community and run her Polish deli empire.

Anonymous threat led to increased security at Dallas Police Department following shooting death of five police officers by a black man during a protest against police killings of black men earlier in the week, with Johnson, a veteran and bomb-making material found in his home. Black Lives Matter organization condemns shootings and plans to continue protests.

Australian Prime Minister Abbott agrees to increase Syrian asylum seekers but not overall refugee numbers; his party members and state premiers call for more action for refugees, with suggestions including temporary housing and a Kosovo-type solution. The Opposition calls for an additional 10,000 places for Middle Eastern refugees, and Labor leader Bill Shorten proposes an extra $A100m for aid. Premier Mike Baird of New South Wales has urged the government to do more than just stop refugees from reaching Australia by boat, with several other states offering to accept more refugees. Australia currently houses about 4,500 Syrian refugees, with a commitment of 13,750 refugees for 2015. The government has faced criticism for its boat-stopping policy, described as "brutal" by the New York Times.

Nigel Farage, UKIP leader, urged a reduction in net migration to around 30,000 people per year and accused the Conservative and Liberal Democrat parties of potentially manipulating a potential EU referendum, arguing that only a UK exit from the EU can achieve this target.

Former England Under-21 manager Gareth Southgate, with prior experience at Middlesbrough and as the FA's head of elite development, is appointed as the permanent England manager. His leadership skills and international football knowledge were key factors in his selection. His first match in charge will be a friendly against Germany on March 22nd.

Apple is resisting the FBI's demand to disable security software on a dead suspect's iPhone, with Mark Zuckerberg and other tech leaders voicing opposition to creating backdoors, while a lawyer for some of the victim's families supports the FBI's demand, anti-virus creator John McAfee has offered to unlock the phone, and the FBI Director argues that this access is necessary to find potential leads related to terrorism.

The article describes the various ways that Queen Elizabeth II celebrated her 90th birthday, including Meeting staff at the Royal Mail delivery office, official events, and a visit by US President Barack Obama and First Lady Michelle Obama. Multiple radio and TV programs, as well as exhibitions, were held to mark the occasion. Members of the royal family expressed their admiration for the Queen's service as monarch and discussed the responsibilities and challenges of their own roles. In a rare interview, Prince William spoke about his approach to his royal duties and his admiration for the Queen as a role model. The article also includes a criticism from a republican pressure group that the BBC's coverage of the Queen's birthday was excessive and one-sided.
