Zachary Quinto, Chris Pine, and John Cho have expressed support for the inclusion of an LGBT character in the Star Trek universe, while George Takei has disagreed, arguing that creator Gene Roddenberry intended for Hikaru Sulu to be heterosexual. Director Justin Lin and Roddenberry's son, Rod Roddenberry, have defended the decision, with Lin stating it was a thoughtful choice and Roddenberry stating his father would have approved. The film Star Trek Beyond, which includes John Cho's character Sulu with a male partner, opens in the UK and Ireland on July 22, coinciding with the 50th anniversary of Star Trek.

Peterborough United defeated Bristol Rovers 4-1, with Jack Marriott scoring a treble and Rory Gaffney scoring a consolation goal for the hosts, while Tom Lockyer hit the bar for Bristol Rovers. The away team had a dominant first half and went ahead early on, and although Rovers had significant second-half opportunities, they were unable to capitalize effectively.

The article reports that jihadists attempted to seize control of strategically important Tadmur on the edge of the ancient city of Palmyra, a UNESCO World Heritage site, but were halted by the Syrian army. The director of Syria's antiquities warned that if IS took control of Palmyra, it would repeat the destruction it had wreaked on other ancient sites in Iraq, prompting fears of an impending "international catastrophe".

On a high-speed train from Amsterdam to Paris, passenger Jamie Robinson accused members of staff of abandoning passengers by locking themselves away in a service room, while the heroic actions of American passengers were widely praised.

GB Taekwondo has selected Muhammad, ranked 59th in the world, for the London Olympics, despite criticism of the decision and threats of legal action from Aaron Cook's camp. The BOA has emphasized the need for improved transparency and communication in athlete selection procedures for future Games.

Hannah Witheridge, 23, and David Miller, 24, were found dead on a beach in Koh Tao, Thailand. The investigation later revealed that the DNA from their bodies did not match that of the Ware brothers, who were initially questioned, and 11 other Burmese people who were questioned in relation to their deaths. The Thai police are now searching for a group of people who were heard singing Western pop songs near the crime scene.

Japan plans to host the 2019 Rugby World Cup and 2020 Olympic Games in Tokyo, focusing on efforts to increase awareness and participation, particularly among young people, using digital media, school programs, and corporate partnerships.

The article discusses the role of army dynamics, particularly the distinction between independent, professional armies and servile armies with a relationship to the autocratic regime, in determining the trajectory of uprisings in Arab countries. The type of army and its relationship to the regime are more important than raw coercive capacity, and ethnic differences among troops can influence their response to protests. Capacity-building without professionalization can lead to more efficient but no less brutal repression.

The unemployment rate hit a record low since 1971 at 5.1%, with 1.68 million people out of work, while average weekly wage growth slowed to 2% and 1.9% including and excluding bonuses respectively. Economic inactivity fell to a record low for women at 27%. These findings are based on the Labour Force Survey.
Middlesbrough beat Bournemouth 2-0, with goals from Stewart Downing and Gastón Ramírez. Bournemouth hit the crossbar twice and were reduced to 10 men after Surman's injury.

Williams driver Felipe Massa suffered two left-rear wheel failures, while Renault's Kevin Magnussen had a suspected broken left rear suspension in the Chinese Grand Prix's first practice session. Both Williams and Renault kept their cars in the pits for the rest of the session, while Lewis Hamilton and Nico Rosberg topped the times. Fernando Alonso returned to McLaren after missing the last race and ended the session 12th fastest. It is unclear if Alonso faced further medical checks during the session.

Hibernian defeated Bonnyrigg Rose 8-1 in a one-sided Scottish Cup match, with three goals from Shinnie, Keatings, and Humphrey in the first half and two from Cummings in the second half. The rout was completed with further goals from Stevenson, Keatings, and Forster. The opening 10 minutes were not evenly matched, and Bonnyrigg was able to score one goal through a penalty.

The article reports that Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni has criticized the parliamentary speaker for passing a bill that expands the Penal Code's ban on male homosexual acts to include female-to-female sex, and makes it illegal to identify as a homosexual or provide services to them. The bill also aims to ban the promotion of homosexuality.

Manager Neil Warnock aims to guide Cardiff City to a top-six finish in the Championship, a feat he considers as the pinnacle of his managerial career, surpassing his previous play-off experiences with Grimsby, Yeovil, and Leyton Orient. He recalls the 2014 Yeovil playoff semi-final against his hometown club Nottingham Forest, where they trailed 2-0 but eventually won 5-4 after extra time. He also acknowledges the hardships and challenges of modern football management, aiming for a 1000-game career milestone.

Scotland, led by Bayern Munich forward Jane Ross, has won all five qualifiers and hosts Iceland on Friday, aiming to secure a place in a major competition after play-off losses for Euro 2013 and the 2019 World Cup. Iceland, also unbeaten, is likely to decide the group winner, with both matches potentially deciding qualification. Ross emphasizes the importance of keeping focus on each step towards the finals, which would be emotional for the team. The team benefits from having 12 players playing in top world leagues, with Ross playing in Germany's Bundesliga.

A former event-rider using a robotic walking suit to regain her independence after a spinal injury, Claire is participating in the London Marathon, which will take her about three weeks to complete, while raising funds for medical research on paralysis and competing against her daughter, Maisie, to see who will walk unaided first.

Jack Walsh, a 23-year-old filmmaker from Northern Ireland, is working for the popular Game Grumps YouTube channel in Los Angeles, helping to coordinate videos, commercials, and potential future TV comedy projects. His passion for film sparked during his A-level course in moving image arts, leading to working with Oscar-nominated composer John Debney, and eventually to his current role at Game Grumps. He hopes to continue advancing his career and potentially return to Northern Ireland's growing film industry in the future.

The Scottish First Minister, Nicola Sturgeon, is ranked 50th on Forbes' 2016 list of the world's most powerful women, with the German Chancellor Angela Merkel topping the list for a sixth year. Specifically, both Sturgeon and Merkel's rankings are due to their leadership and actions in national and international politics. The list includes other notable female figures in influential positions, including Hillary Clinton, Janet Yellen, the Queen, and Mary Barra of General Motors.

The findings of a study published in Conservation Biology revealed that many mammals perceive ultra-violet (UV) light, including reindeer, and avoid power lines due to the UV emissions from bursts of charge. This avoidance, researchers suggest, could be disrupting habitat and migration patterns, and as these coronas occur on all power lines, the global impact on wildlife is significant.

A former employee told the BBC that staff at Kids Company in Southwark were informed of complaints about a client who sexually assaulted girls he met there, but did not pass on the concerns or alert authorities. The charity states it would have reported any known allegation to the police, while an ongoing investigation by the Metropolitan Police is taking place.

Paul Austin, a Brexit supporter who runs an interior fitting-out business, now questions his initial decision to support Brexit as he expresses concerns about immigration policies, quality checks for imported goods, and limitations for ordinary citizens to seek international court help, citing the Charlie Gard case and the Grenfell Tower fire as examples.

England came close to a famous win on the subcontinent, with Adil Rashid taking five wickets in the second innings to help bowl out Pakistan for a lower-than-expected 378. However, England fell 25 runs short of the target of 74, with their unusual batting order struggling to score quickly enough under the pressure of Pakistan's disciplined fielding and spin from both ends.

Celtic manager Rodgers praised the performances of newly signed French youth international Ntcham and 19-year-old Kundai Benyu, stating they could be significant players for the team. He also noted that he may change his plans for sending Benyu on loan, considering keeping him with the first team instead. The team lost 4-0 to Lyon in a friendly match but Rodgers was content with the exercise and performance levels.

The article discusses the upcoming arrival of a potential preventative Ebola vaccine in Liberia, produced by GlaxoSmithKline and the US National Institutes of Health. The vaccine is expected to be administered to volunteers in a trial involving up to 30,000 people, with results comparing its effectiveness to placebos and other experimental vaccines. The vaccine is still in development and the World Health Organization and other regulators will need to approve its safety and effectiveness before mass immunization campaigns can be considered, due to the decreasing number of Ebola cases.
In the article, both Blackpool and Wycombe Wanderers have multiple chances, with numerous shots narrowly missing the mark or being blocked, but neither team could find a goal, ending in a 0-0 draw.

A $70 million settlement has been reached by the Australian government to avoid a court trial over allegations of harm suffered by 1,905 asylum seekers held on PNG's Manus Island between 2012 and 2016, with the settlement intended as a cost-effective alternative to the potential costs and uncertainties of a trial for its offshore detention policy. The status of the asylum seekers who were held on Manus Island during that time period is unclear.

Paul Scholes, the legendary midfielder who spent his entire 20-year career at Manchester United and won numerous titles, returned from retirement after 12 years to play for the team during a match against Manchester City. Scholes played for 31 minutes, contributing to the team's 3-2 victory, and has a success rate of 90.2% in the Premier League for passing. Prior to his retirement in 2013, Scholes played his final match in the Champions League final and won 66 England caps.

A Welsh creator born in south Wales, who moved to California in 1989, created SuperTed as a bedtime story and later turned it into a successful TV series, books, and films. He is currently planning a new series of SuperTed in Wales, working on a film about the late legendary Cardiff City player Robin Friday, and has produced an animated film, Norm Of The North, using CGI technology.

The rise of right-wing, nationalist parties across Europe, such as Austria's Freedom Party (FPOe), Denmark's Danish People's Party (DPP), Finland's Finns Party, France's National Front (FN), Germany's Alternative for Germany (AfD), Greece's Golden Dawn, Hungary's Jobbik, Italy's Northern League (Lega Nord), and the Netherlands' Party for Freedom (PVV), among others, is reshaping Europe's political landscape by capitalizing on discontent about immigration, globalization, and the perceived weakness of the establishment. These parties often advocate for stricter immigration policies, anti-EU sentiment, and traditional national values.

Spurs chairman Daniel Levy defended limited summer transfers, while Chelsea manager Antonio Conte questioned Tottenham's spending strategy, suggesting that they should buy expensive players to compete with top teams.

A total of 387 disruptive passengers were arrested at UK airports in the period from February 2016 to February 2017, a significant increase from the 255 arrests the previous year. A voluntary code of conduct introduced in 2016 aims to address disruptive passenger behavior, but its effectiveness is questioned by some cabin crew. Airlines UK advocates for a ban on passengers consuming their own alcohol on planes, and low-cost airline Jet2 has already instituted this policy. The Home Office is considering recommendations to strengthen alcohol regulations at airports, including revoking their exemption from the Licensing Act. The Airport Operators Association claims they sell alcohol responsibly.

The British Racing Drivers' Club (BRDC) has exercised a break clause in its contract for the British Grand Prix after 2019, potentially causing the race to move from its long-time home at Silverstone, due to financial losses, but Formula 1 is still negotiating with the BRDC for the race to continue at Silverstone, with interest in other UK options yet to be specified.

Manchester United's 18-year-old Marcus Rashford scored a late winner to secure a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Hull City, with Jose Mourinho's team maintaining their perfect start to the Premier League season alongside Chelsea. Rashford's goal was the climax to a performance of persistence and intelligence from the visitors, with Rashford and Henrikh Mkhitaryan causing problems for the Hull defense. Hull lacked numbers but showed spirit with Sam Clucas impressing in midfield and Adama Diomande and Abel Hernandez chasing hard in attack. The result means Manchester United extended their unbeaten run to three games, while Hull's 100% start to their top-flight campaign is over.

Ben Stokes, who infamously missed the 2014 World Twenty20 due to a disciplinary incident, has been named vice-captain of the Test team and has expressed his desire to maintain his aggressive style, while acknowledging the need to temper it at times. He is currently participating in his first series since becoming the Indian Premier League's most expensive foreign player. England, fresh off a strong run against West Indies, expect a tough challenge in their upcoming match, as West Indies, with a relatively inexperienced team, aim to prove their talent despite being ranked ninth in the world in 50-over cricket.

At Coventry City College, staff with backgrounds in vocational trades have been teaching GCSE English and maths to underachieving students to help them advance in their careers. Despite minimal success with these subjects in school, students like Reece Beal and Samantha Richards are now showing promise in their field of study. The new approach, which includes hiring maths graduates and retraining veteran teachers, has generated strong results in preparation for vocational qualifications.

A Welsh Transport Minister has expressed concern about the status of autumn leaf clearance by Network Rail, alleging insufficient investment has led to maintenance issues on train wheels causing overcrowding and reduced train availability, a situation described as a "national crisis" by Plaid Cymru's Adam Price. Network Rail has responded that they are working together with Welsh authorities to maximize value for taxpayers' money.

The hour-long session of the Welsh Affairs Select Committee addressed questions on Brexit, steel, devolution, and the Severn crossings, with Secretary of State for Wales Alun Cairns emphasizing potential opportunities in Brexit for Welsh trade, maintaining the status quo on devolution and the Barnett Formula, and committing to a fiscal framework for steelmaking.

Durham Jets pulled off a three-wicket victory against Leicestershire, overcoming a powerful start from Luke Ronchi, while Hampshire won by 24 runs in Bristol. Several matches were hampered by heavy rain.

China, under the leadership of Mao Zedong, transitioned from a stagnant communist regime to a fast-growing economy following Mao's death in 1976 and subsequent economic reforms. Today, China has the world's second-largest economy, attracting foreign investment while also investing billions abroad. However, human rights groups accuse the Chinese authorities of persecuting ethnic minorities, including Tibetans and Uighurs, and of systematic destruction of Tibetan Buddhist culture, particularly in Tibet.

Betting has been suspended on Ellie Goulding to perform a song for the upcoming James Bond film, Spectre, due to a cryptic Instagram post that suggests she has been working at Abbey Road Studios, a location where James Bond theme songs have been recorded in the past.

The Scottish government, under the leadership of Nicola Sturgeon, is planning for a referendum on Scottish independence in the future, particularly if Scotland's position in Europe is compromised, but a vote is not expected in 2017. The current discussions revolve around the possibility of a "soft Brexit," where the UK remains in the EU single market, which could potentially delay or negate the need for a referendum.

Four individuals, Bakr Hamad, Shahif Kadir, Zana Rahim, and Awat Hamasalih, from various UK cities, refused to consent to extradition on charges of international terrorism for allegedly plotting to free Mullah Krekar, a suspected leader of a "jihadist network" Rawti Shax (or Didi Nwe), aiming to establish a caliphate in Iraq's Kurdistan region. Arrests were made in six European countries, primarily targeting an international recruiting pipeline sending jihadists to join proscribed terrorist organizations Islamic State and Al-Nusra in Iraq and Syria. No specific threat to the UK was suggested. The suspects may challenge their extradition based on the risk of "refoulement" due to the potential violation of their rights as refugees.

The IFS's Green Budget forecasts a 14.1% reduction in departmental spending over the next four years, resulting in the lowest share of public spending since at least 1948, fewer people working in the public sector since 1971, and projected economic growth of 3% this year. The upcoming election will present a choice between a Conservative or Tory-led government pursuing fiscal consolidation through spending cuts, and a Labour government potentially prioritizing investments in infrastructure spending. The IFS does not explicitly state that it is optimistic about UK growth.

In the football match between Cambridge United and Cheltenham Town, Luke Berry scored a hat-trick, while Uche Ikpeazu and Greg Taylor provided assists, but Billy Waters managed to score a consolation goal for Cheltenham Town in a 3-1 loss.

A controversial bonfire in a public car park in Belfast, funded by public tax money, has sparked controversy due to the burning of political flags and materials considered distasteful. The bonfire is defended as part of loyalist culture, but the PSNI is investigating complaints about distasteful materials found on various bonfires. Meanwhile, Sinn Féin considers the burning of flags and election posters on bonfires to be a hate crime.

The article discusses how broadcasters are using technology to engage viewers, notably through companion apps for shows like The Walking Dead and Sons of Anarchy, which allow viewers to predict outcomes, track conversations on social media, and interact with exclusive content. The apps use audio watermarking and similar technologies to synchronize with the show and provide a second-screen experience.

The article discusses the political pressure on tech companies like Facebook and Google to remove hateful content from their platforms, particularly in light of a terrorist attack in Finsbury Park mosque. However, it raises concerns over the difficulties in managing vast amounts of content, jurisdictional issues, and the potential for censorship by private companies with global influence. The author argues that while tech companies should assume responsibility, the implications of their increased involvement in policing online content must be carefully considered.

The article depicts Longford Town Centre, initially conceived as a symbol of Ireland's economic success during the boom years, now embodying the challenges of the country's economic decline. Local retailer Matt O'Brien attributes his improved business to expanding into children's clothing and a substantial dress-hire service. Criticism is directed towards the government for not adequately addressing the region's issues, particularly concerning investment, job creation, and parking, with Fianna Fáil arguing that funds meant for water meters should be used to enhance broadband instead. The prospective €200 million Center Parcs tourism development in Ballymahon offers optimism, but additional measures remain necessary for stimulating local trade, as acknowledged by merchants like Matt O'Brien, who desires free parking to draw more customers to the town.

The experimental aircraft, Solar Impulse, with a wingspan larger than a jumbo jet and weighing only as much as a large car, piloted by Bertrand Borschberg, embarked on a 5-6 day solo sun-powered flight from Nanjing, China, aiming to cross the Pacific Ocean en route to Hawaii, a journey expected to set new records for single-seater aircraft durations. The mission, dubbed less as a pioneering aviation advancement, but more as a showcase of clean technologies, has encountered multiple delays due to weather conditions and is being carefully monitored and managed from a control room in Monaco.

Lord Carey, a former Archbishop of Canterbury, has expressed support for the Assisted Dying Bill, citing the case of Tony Nicklinson as a significant influencing factor, despite concerns raised by Justin Welby and others regarding potential pressures on vulnerable individuals.

The article presents a collection of various tweets and opinions of different people regarding how to prevent North Korea's recent nuclear test from escalating into an international crisis, with ideas ranging from enforcing sanctions, inviting North Korea to international talks, greater UN involvement, and considering former NBA basketball player Dennis Rodman as a potential mediator due to his personal relationships with North Korean leaders.

Refugees and asylum seekers living in Belfast work with the Mourne Heritage Trust to rebuild dry-stone walls and repair mountain paths in the Mournes, County Down, as part of a volunteer program that provides them with a tranquil retreat, improves their language skills, and allows them to make new friends while also benefiting the Trust with free labor for preserving the area's natural beauty.

Stuart Broad's exceptional 5-wicket haul in a single spell, under challenging conditions, along with England's team efforts, turned the third day of the match from a position of 75 runs behind into a victory, stunning South Africa who had started the series ranked number one. This was a reaffirmation of England's growing prowess in Test cricket.

The detailed mapping of groundwater reserves across Africa indicates vast reserves in northern Africa, enough to sustain low-yielding water supplies for drinking and community irrigation, particularly in areas with limited rainfall. The study encourages careful exploration and sustainable development of boreholes for water extraction.

Lord O'Donnell, a former UK cabinet secretary, suggests that it is uncertain whether the UK will fully separate from the EU in the near future, given the potential impact of public opinion and EU changes on the process. He also highlights the challenges involved in making Brexit happen, including the possibility that the EU may not undergo radical changes to accommodate the UK's continued membership.

A 22-year-old woman, Sian O'Callaghan, has gone missing, and a search led by local volunteers and police is underway in Savernake Forest near Marlborough. CCTV footage of her last known movements has been released, and a £20,000 reward has been offered for information leading to her whereabouts.

Ferrari showed promising pace during the second practice session for the Chinese Grand Prix, with Kimi Raikkonen leading Mercedes driver Lewis Hamilton by a margin. Hamilton, who has a five-place grid penalty, expressed optimism about the upcoming race, stating it would be a challenging but exciting fight. Fernando Alonso, returning from illness, ranked 11th, with teammate Jenson Button not far behind. The session saw no repeat of previous wheel failures experienced by some drivers. While Ferrari's performance might suggest a potential challenge to Mercedes, it's important to note their history of inconsistent performance this season.

Arlene Foster is joining a campaign calling on Germany to acknowledge its moral and financial responsibility towards Thalidomide survivors, who were born with birth defects due to the drug and are seeking compensation for their struggles. A representative of the campaign, Kim Fenton, a former mayor in Northern Ireland, shares her personal battle with the drug's long-term effects, including dislocated hips, deteriorating health, and financial strain.

Actor Eli Wallach, born in 1915 to Polish Jewish immigrants, had a varied career on stage and screen from the 1950s until his death in 2016. Known for roles in films such as The Magnificent Seven, The Good, the Bad and the Ugly, and How the West Was Won, Wallach received an honorary Oscar in 2011 for his versatile and memorable performances. He continued acting into his 90s, with roles in TV shows including Batman and Nurse Jackie. He graduated from the University of Texas and studied at the Actors' Studio before making his Broadway debut in 1945. Wallach was married to actress Anne Jackson for 65 years.

almost 10% of Hanson Academy students were sent home for uniform non-compliance on Tuesday, and over 63 were sent home on Wednesday, according to principal Elizabeth Churton. Parents, including Caren Oxlaide and Diane Hickey, criticized the strict policy, citing financial difficulties and disagreements over shoe interpretation. The school insists it will continue the policy and plans to work with struggling parents.

Violence erupted in Beirut between Sunni pro- and anti-Syrian groups following the shooting death of two anti-Syrian clerics, marking the first such incident in Beirut since Syria's conflict began last year. Despite deep divisions over Syria, Lebanon has thus far managed to avoid more widespread violence, but Sunday's incident could escalate tensions.

Nick Clegg argues during his campaign that only a stable and strong coalition involving his party can save the country from another election, due to the hardening positions of Labour and the Conservatives on coalition deals, potentially leading to an unstable minority government. He also defends his party against claims of cutting too deeply and excessive borrowing by both the Conservatives and Labour.

Liverpool suffered a stunning second-half collapse in the Europa League final, losing 3-1 to Sevilla and missing out on Champions League football next season. Manager Jürgen Klopp conceded the performance was below par and promises to address the issues and return stronger. Former Liverpool defender Mark Lawrenson was critical of the Reds' defensive performance, particularly left-back Alberto Moreno. Lawrenson expects a significant summer of changes at Anfield.

In the West Midlands, a man named Ikram Elahi was killed, and three others were injured, with a 25-year-old in critical condition, following a violent incident in Sparkbrook involving a gun and knives. Over 200 to 300 individuals were reported to have gathered in the area prior to the incident, and the police have arrested four suspects for violent disorder and one for drug possession. Community leaders have expressed concerns about the ongoing violence.

South African banks, including Barclays, JP Morgan, and HSBC, are under investigation for alleged currency manipulation involving online chat rooms, with the competition commission calling for fines of 10% of each bank's annual turnover in the country. President Jacob Zuma has welcomed the investigation and is committed to addressing market distortions and diversifying the financial sector. The scandal has the potential to further damage the banking sector's reputation due to South Africa's ongoing economic crisis and a history of foreign exchange scandals. Opposition parties have mixed views on the case.

A parliamentarian accused Arlene Foster's economic advisors Timothy Johnston and Mr. Robinson of having interests in the poultry industry that prevented him from reducing the tariff on the Renewable Heat Incentive (RHI) scheme. Both advisors denied these allegations, stating that they had no personal or family connections to the poultry industry. MLA Jonathan Bell made the claims under parliamentary privilege.

The development of a molecular "tape recorder" using CRISPR gene editing technology has the potential to revolutionize developmental biology by providing a compact, inherited record of a cell's history, enabling researchers to trace cell lineages in complex tissues and organs, thereby offering profound insights into biological development and the origins of diseases.

The man was denied permission to stop the department's plan to publish another list of RHI recipients, with the court deeming the potential damage to his reputation as "tenuous," and the department intending to differentiate between capped and earlier, more generous tariff recipients by including the date of application in the information to be published.

Judge Thokozile Masipa sentenced Oscar Pistorius to five years in jail for culpable homicide for shooting and killing his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp, following trial proceedings that spanned several months. The defense expects the athlete, an amputee sprinter, to serve about 10 months, with the remainder under house arrest. He was taken to the hospital wing in a prison in Pretoria for a medical assessment. Pistorius' family stated they won't appeal the sentence. The Steenkamps expressed relief that the case was over, while the Women's League of South Africa's ruling African National Congress plans to appeal, arguing that a five-year sentence sends a message that it's fine to commit heinous crimes like femicide. The International Paralympic Committee prohibits Pistorius from participating in any events for five years, regardless of possible early release. The trial exposed South Africa's gun culture, police, and prison inadequacies, and is widely seen as the fall of a global icon.

The beach where Tunisia's worst terror attack occurred has reopened, yet emotional scars remain for those impacted, particularly 57-year-old Sabi who lost several customers. The tourism industry faces a severe threat as holidaymakers leave, with many staying put but feeling anxious. The attack has added to Tunisians' ongoing concern over Islamist attacks, as the birthplace of the Arab Spring now struggles to combat rising extremism andporous borders enabling radical militants to cross into neighboring countries like Libya. The new coalition government is working to quell the violence, but the damage done to tourism may threaten Tunisia's economy.

British Foreign Secretary Philip Hammond's visit to Tripoli mainly aims to support the nascent Government of National Accord in Libya, providing aid worth £10 million and offering further practical assistance to combat people smuggling, terrorism, and instability, which threatens southern Europe. The potential involvement of British special forces in Libya and the possibility of a European force under Italian command remain topics of speculation, with concerns about the safety of such forces in the face of local militias and IS. The future support will likely focus on training the Libyan police, coastguard, and military, with the EU coordinating a significant portion of this. The new government's need for international backing is critical, as Libya's instability has become a major concern for southern Europe and beyond.

The Beyond Caravaggio exhibition at the National Galleries of Scotland showcases masterpieces by Michelangelo Merisi da Caravaggio, including The Taking of Christ (1602), which was rediscovered in Dublin in 1990 and previously owned by Scottish country gentleman William Hamilton Nisbet. The exhibition, featuring works by artists such as Gentileschi, Ribera, and Spadarino, also includes Ribera's The Martyrdom of St Bartholomew (1634) on loan from the National Gallery of Art in Washington. Beyond Caravaggio runs from June 17 to September 24 and tickets cost Â£12.

Two men, Virgilio Correia (aged 35) and Christopher Menaul (aged 27), were sentenced to at least 16 and 9 years in prison respectively for the murder of Wing Fu Cheung (64) in January 2015, as well as additional time for wounding with intent and robbery. Portuguese national Correia and Menaul had attacked Cheung and his wife Kam-Fung (known as Winnie) as they drove home after closing their restaurant, taking cash, bank cards, electronics, and more from Winnie. Winnie returned to Hong Kong with the couple's children following the murder. Gary and Lisa Thompson, who assisted the killers by providing them refuge, cleaning facilities, and removing clothing, were also sentenced for their part in the crime.

County cricket is undergoing changes, including less Championship matches, a simplified division structure, T20 Blast during school summer holidays, and a Lord's one-day knockout final in July, to make it more appealing to younger audiences and secure its future against the potential city franchise model. The changes aim to reduce the number of games, improve skill development, and encourage more people to play and watch county cricket. Notable figures like Kevin Howells and Michael Vaughan advocate for better television coverage for the T20 Blast.

US economy growth for Q4 was 2.6% (lower than the projected 3%), but consumer spending saw a significant rise of 4.3% due to reduced fuel prices, marking the fastest rate in almost nine years. Economist Mark Zandi is optimistic about the economy's recovery, expecting a large portion of growth for the year to come from personal savings on lowered fuel prices. However, business investment is declining, which raised concerns about the sustainability of the economic upturn, with some economists predicting a possible delay in raising interest rates until late 2015 or early 2016.

The article states that the delay in devolving Corporation Tax to Northern Ireland, due to the failure of the Welfare Reform Bill, is causing uncertainty for businesses, potentially affecting their investment decisions and job creation in the region. The proposed rate for Corporation Tax in Northern Ireland is not explicitly stated in the article, only that it has previously been suggested that the rate could match Ireland's 12.5%.

Chris Rea, a multi-million album-selling singer-songwriter, gained a unique perspective on Formula 1 after helping driver Eddie Irvine with tire changes during the 1995 Monaco Grand Prix. His love for F1 began as a child watching the race on TV, where he became fascinated with Wolfgang Alexander von Trips. Later, he discovered and shared previously unseen footage of von Trips. This experience led him to release a rereleased double-album and DVD, "La Passione," featuring Von Trips' archival footage. His passion for F1 remains strong, though he feels the current state of the sport lacks the appeal of its past. His homage to the sport includes a police-themed Morris Minor and memories of watching Ayrton Senna race in underpowered machinery. Despite having given up his Ferrari, circumstances such as its size and Italian reliability issues, he still holds F1 in high regard, particularly the iconic red cars.

Margaret Thatcher, famously known as the "Iron Lady," served as the UK's prime minister for 11 years (1979-1990), where she implemented significant reforms such as privatization, housing policy, and economic policies that transformed Britain into a thriving global financial hub. Her tenure was marked by divisive opinions, as her policies were met with both support and opposition, including protests, riots, and the infamous Miners' Strike of 1984. Known for her determination and resilience, Thatcher was the longest-serving prime minister of the 20th century before resigning due to party pressure and is remembered as one of the most influential figures in modern British history.

The mental health tribunal has decided that Ian Stewart Brady, the notorious serial killer who tortured and murdered multiple children in the 1960s, is still suffering from a treatable mental disorder and needs continued treatment at Ashworth Hospital. Brady's request to be transferred to a Scottish prison has been denied.

A member of Fifa's Ad-Hoc Electoral Committee, Domenico Scala, is being challenged by the Liberian Football Association (LFA) to step down from his role due to a potential conflict of interest as he shares nationality with candidate Gianni Infantino in the upcoming election to replace President Sepp Blatter. The LFA has threatened to take the case to the Court of Arbitration for Sport if Scala does not step down by Thursday, but Scala maintains that there is no conflict of interest as there is no incumbent President in this election.

Brock Turner, a former swimming champion, was released from jail after serving a third of his six-year sentence for sexually assaulting a woman outside Stanford University, sparking calls for reform in California's sexual assault laws.

The trial of Stephen Beadman and Luke Harlow is ongoing at Nottingham Crown Court, where both men are charged with false imprisonment in the death of Kayleigh Haywood. Harlow had earlier pleaded guilty to sexual grooming, two counts of sexual activity with a child, and attempting to meet two other underage girls for sexual purposes. The prosecution alleges that on the night of November 13th, 2016, Kayleigh went willingly to Harlow's flat in Ibstock, believing they were in a secret relationship. She was given substantial amounts of alcohol, sexually touched, and falsely imprisoned by Harlow, while Beadman was alleged to have held her against her will as well. Kayleigh tried to escape the flat at one point, and was later found dead with head and facial injuries.

The BBC article discusses the UK's European Union (EU) vote, with a focus on the significant divide between London and the north of England, Scotland, and various regions in England. The northern parts strongly voted to leave the EU, while many London voters and some areas in Scotland voted to remain. The disconnect is perceived as a vote against the metropolitan elite and establishment. The article also highlights the potential implications of the vote in each region, including the possibility of Scottish independence, economic uncertainty, and the return of border checks in areas like Northern Ireland.

Train workers are set to strike for 24 hours starting Monday evening over pay and job disputes, leading to limited or cancelled services on Scotrail, Gatwick and Heathrow Express lines, Southeastern, Virgin West Coast Mainline, East Coast line, CrossCountry Trains, Chiltern Railways, Arriva Trains Wales and First Great Western. The strike could affect football fans traveling for the Championship play-off final at Wembley. Talks between unions and Network Rail continue, with further disruptions and delays anticipated on Wednesday. Passengers are advised to check with their operators and avoid traveling unless necessary.

The Rugby Football Union (RFU) proposes shortening the Six Nations tournament from seven weeks to six, causing concerns about player safety and the potential impact on physical and training demands. An independent review is being undertaken regarding a controversial Six Nations game between Wales and France, involving a head injury assessment controversy.

Scottish Labour Party leader Johann Lamont resigned, accusing the UK party leadership of treating Scotland as a "branch office" and not recognizing the Scottish party's need for autonomy, a charge echoed by former Scottish Labour leaders Jack McConnell and Henry McLeish. The trio demanded answers from UK party leader Ed Miliband and supporters.

Club Brugge became Belgian champions for the first time in 11 years, Benfica secured a third consecutive Portuguese title, Besiktas were crowned Turkish champions, Stuttgart was relegated from the German Bundesliga, Steven Fletcher marked his possible last Ligue 1 game for Marseille, Sevilla ended the season without an away league win, Sporting Gijon avoided relegation in La Liga, and Palermo secured their Serie A survival. Meanwhile, Francesco Totti's future at Roma remains uncertain.

The National Audit Office report finds that the Department for Education overshot its budgeted £7.3bn for academies by £1bn over two years due to insufficient preparations and inadequate oversight, leading to increased spending for temporary funding of non-academy schools and other budget reallocations.

The government requirement for key nursery workers to have at least a grade C in GCSE English and maths has caused a decline in enrollments on Level 3 courses and a potential nursery staffing shortage and recruitment crisis, threatening the quality of childcare and government plans for free childcare. Industry leaders suggest recognizing equivalent qualifications and a focus on skills and experience to address the issue.

Donald Trump's presidential campaign statements included support for strong interrogation methods like waterboarding and a desire for Mexico to pay for a border wall, restrictions on Muslim immigration, and skepticism of climate change science, among other views. Some positions have been adjusted since the campaign.
